#### ROUT-15: `WINDOW_CAPACITY` bounds only the Bloom sizing — `exact` and `ring` are unbounded within the window
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `d0ac125`  ·  2026-08-26
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/dedup_cache.rs:21-22, 36, 53-60`
- **What:** `WINDOW_CAPACITY = 200_000` is used solely as the Bloom's `capacity` argument (line 36). Neither `exact: HashSet<MessageId>` nor `ring: VecDeque<(MessageId, Instant)>` is capped; `record` pushes unconditionally and eviction is purely time-based (1 h).
- **Evidence:**
```
21	/// Rolling window capacity for the message-id bloom.
22	const WINDOW_CAPACITY: usize = 200_000;
...
36	            bloom: BloomFilter::new(WINDOW_CAPACITY, BLOOM_FPR),
...
53	    pub fn record(&mut self, id: MessageId) {
54	        self.bloom.insert(id.to_bytes());
55	        self.exact.insert(id);
56	        self.ring.push_back((id, Instant::now()));
57	        self.evict_old();
58	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The name and doc comment ("Rolling window capacity") promise a bound on the window; the structure honours it for the Bloom only. Beyond 200 k entries per hour the Bloom's FPR also exceeds the documented 0.1 %.
- **Root cause:** The constant was introduced for Bloom sizing and mistaken for a structural cap.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A node forwarding 1 M distinct messages per hour (achievable by an attacker minting message ids over a fast transport) holds 1 M × (16 B `MessageId` in `exact` + hash-set slack, plus 16 B + 16 B `Instant` in `ring`) ≈ 100 MB for a full hour.
- **Impact:** Attacker-driven RAM spike bounded only by message rate × 1 h.
- **Fix:** Enforce `while self.ring.len() > WINDOW_CAPACITY { pop_front + exact.remove }` in `record`, in addition to the time-based eviction.

#### ROUT-16: `RoutingTable::new` silently discards its `expiry` argument
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `440f610` (subsumed by ROUT-12/13 — `RoutingTable` now stores `expiry: Duration`)  ·  2026-08-26
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/known_path.rs:33-35` (fn `new`)
- **What:** The constructor takes `_expiry: Duration` and returns `RoutingTable::default()`. The value is dropped; the struct has no expiry field. Expiry is instead re-supplied at every `prune_expired(expiry)` call, so two call sites can disagree and nothing detects it.
- **Evidence:**
```
33	    pub fn new(_expiry: Duration) -> Self {
34	        RoutingTable::default()
35	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** A configuration knob that looks load-bearing (every call site passes a meaningful value: `mod.rs:110` passes 600 s, `known_path.rs:132/150/164` pass 600 s, `known_path.rs:173` passes 10 ms) but is inert. `RoutingEngine` works around it by keeping a *second* copy in `table_ttl` (`mod.rs:98, 111`).

- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `known_path.rs:171-178` (`prune_expired_entries`) constructs with 10 ms and prunes with 10 ms, so it passes. A caller that constructs with 60 s and calls `engine.prune()` gets the engine's 600 s instead — silently, with no compile error.
- **Impact:** Misconfiguration that cannot be diagnosed from the call site; two sources of truth for the same TTL.
- **Fix:** Store `expiry` in the struct and have `prune_expired(&mut self)` take no argument; drop `RoutingEngine::table_ttl`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `mod.rs:97-98, 110-111, 300`; `known_path.rs` tests.

#### ROUT-17: Flood has no fan-out cap and ignores `hop_count` — free amplification for any sender
- **Severity:** Medium  *(as filed: High — corrected by adversarial verification)*
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED-BUT-DOWNGRADED. See §14.

- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/flood.rs:42-73` (fn `recipients_for_flood`)
- **What:** The `_hop_count` parameter is prefixed-underscore and completely unused — the recipient set does not narrow as the message travels. There is also no maximum on `recipients.len()`: every LinkedUp neighbor gets a copy. A node with `d` neighbors produces `d−1` copies per hop with no rate limit, no priority-based fan-out reduction, and (per ROUT-4) no dedup.
- **Evidence:**
```
42	pub async fn recipients_for_flood(
43	    neighbor_table: &NeighborTable,
44	    sender: PeerId,
45	    already_flooded: &[PeerId],
46	    _hop_count: u8,
...
69	            recipients.push(nb.peer_id);
70	        }
71	    }
72	    recipients
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `CONGESTION_CONTROL.md:204` — *"To prevent a single node from flooding the mesh"* — specifies a per-sender token bucket (10/min for P4+); `CONGESTION_CONTROL.md:247-266` specifies per-transport `ForwardingRecord` tracking so the same message is never sent twice to the same neighbor on the same transport. Neither exists here. The signature advertises hop-awareness it does not have.
- **Root cause:** `hop_count` was threaded into the signature for a planned fan-out taper that was never implemented; the parameter was silenced with `_` rather than removed, hiding the gap.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** 200-device shelter, average degree 12, P1 message (`max_hops = 5`). One injected message yields up to `11^5 ≈ 161,000` radio transmissions. - **Fix:** (a) Remove `_hop_count` or use it: `let fanout = policy_fanout(priority).saturating_sub(hop_count as usize).max(1)`; (b) cap `recipients` to a `MAX_FLOOD_FANOUT` (e.g. 8), selecting the highest-quality links via `LinkRecord::quality`; (c) wire the per-sender token bucket from `CONGESTION_CONTROL.md:204-243`.

#### ROUT-18: `max_hops_for_priority(P0) = u8::MAX` — "unlimited" is a 255-hop amplification budget on the one class an attacker forges
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `4bb4733`  ·  2026-08-26
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/flood.rs:26-31` (fn `max_hops_for_priority`)
- **What:** P0 maps to `u8::MAX`, commented "unlimited". Combined with `mod.rs:252` (`hop_count < policy.max_hops`) a P0 message is flooded for up to 255 hops. In a mesh of diameter ~5 that is 250 hops of pure re-amplification.
- **Evidence:**
```
26	    let max_hops = match p {
27	        MessagePriority::P0 => u8::MAX, // unlimited
28	        MessagePriority::P1 | MessagePriority::P2 | MessagePriority::P3 => 5,
29	        MessagePriority::P4 | MessagePriority::P5 | MessagePriority::P6 | MessagePriority::P7 => 3,
30	    };
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `BASELINE_ROUTING.md` §Algorithm 3 does say *"unlimited for P0"*, but its stated rationale — *"prevents messages from circulating forever in loops and consuming bandwidth/storage indefinitely"* — is defeated for exactly the highest-value class. `crates/iris-core/src/message_engine/mod.rs:1451-1457` documents the same concern verbatim (*"255 is not a meaningful bound for a mesh and P0 is exactly the class an attacker would forge"*) and explicitly defers the fix to the routing design owners — i.e. to this function.
- **Root cause:** Spec says "unlimited"; `u8` cannot express it, so `u8::MAX` was used as a sentinel and then treated as a real bound by `mod.rs:252`.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Attacker forges a P0 envelope with no `max_hops`. Every relay recomputes `hop_cap` = 255 (`message_engine/mod.rs:1458-1460`). With ROUT-4 (no dedup) and ROUT-17 (no fan-out cap) this is unbounded mesh-wide amplification for as long as the TTL permits.
- **Impact:** Worst-case DoS amplification is concentrated on the emergency traffic class.
- **Fix:** Set the P0 ceiling to a real mesh diameter bound (e.g. 12–16) and represent "unlimited" — if genuinely required — as `Option<u8>`/an explicit `Unlimited` variant so the sentinel is not silently reused as a hop count.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `message_engine/mod.rs:1458`, `sim/mod.rs:323, 698`, `opportunistic.rs:70-80` (`l_for_priority` mins against this value), `flood.rs:186-192` tests, `EMERG_DESIGN.md` policy sign-off.

```
234	        }
235	        // Algorithm 2: Known path (validate next-hop reachability).
236	        if let Some(decision) =
237	            try_known_path(recipient, &mut self.routing_table, neighbor_table).await
238	        {
239	            return decision;
240	        }
...
252	        if hop_count < policy.max_hops {
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `decide`'s own doc comment (`mod.rs:185-186`) states *"Hop count must not reach the priority-based cap, shared with the flood module."* `BASELINE_ROUTING.md` §Correctness — *"At hop_count=0, drop"* — is a global message property, not a flood-only one.
- **Root cause:** The hop check was placed inside the flood branch (mirroring the spec's `flood_with_hop_limit` pseudo-code) rather than as a chain precondition.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Two nodes A and B each hold a stale `RouteEntry` for D naming the other as next hop (easy to arrange via ROUT-12). A message for D ping-pongs A→B→A→… `decide` returns `KnownPath` every time regardless of `hop_count`. In production `message_engine/mod.rs:947-948` saves this by checking `hop_cap` before relaying, but the routing engine's own API contract does not hold, and any other consumer (SIM, FFI, a future dispatcher) inherits an unbounded loop.
- **Impact:** Routing loop confined only by an external caller's discipline; the "no loops" correctness guarantee is not a property of this module.
- **Fix:** Hoist the check to the top of `decide_inner`: `if hop_count >= max_hops_for_priority(priority).max_hops { return ForwardingDecision::Store; }` (or `Drop` when also TTL-expired, per ROUT-6). Direct delivery to the final recipient may legitimately be exempted — but that must be an explicit, commented carve-out.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `mod.rs:400-411` test (`hop_budget_exhausted_stores`) already asserts the Store outcome for a bare table; add cases where the recipient/known path exists at `hop_count == max_hops`.

#### ROUT-20: Every flood decision deep-clones every neighbor's ~175 KB Bloom filter
- **Severity:** Medium  *(as filed: High — corrected by adversarial verification)*
- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED-BUT-DOWNGRADED. For the routing occurrence; the `gateway/mod.rs:673` occurrence should be split out as its own finding, since gateway code is reachable. See §14.
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `ec150a6`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/flood.rs:51` (fn `recipients_for_flood`)
- **What:** `neighbor_table.neighbors().await` is `self.inner.lock().await.values().cloned().collect()` (`neighbor_table.rs:227-229`). `Neighbor` is `#[derive(Clone)]` and holds `peer_bloom: Option<BloomFilter>` (`neighbor_table.rs:49`), and `BloomFilter` is `#[derive(Clone)]` over `bits: Vec<u8>` (`dedup.rs:86-90`). `BloomFilter::default()` is sized `BLOOM_CAPACITY = 100_000` at `BLOOM_FPR = 0.001` → `bloom_bits` ≈ 1,437,760 bits ≈ **175 KB per neighbor**. The routing code needs only `peer_id`, `state` and `links`.
- **Evidence:**
```
51	    for neighbor in neighbor_table.neighbors().await {
52	        let nb = neighbor;
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `BASELINE_ROUTING.md` §Resource Budget: *"Algorithm 3 (flood, 10 neighbors) | <1 ms | 0.1 %"*. Cloning 10 × 175 KB = 1.75 MB of heap allocation + memcpy per decision is orders of magnitude over that on a Pi Zero / phone, and it happens while the neighbor-table mutex is held.
- **Root cause:** A convenience snapshot API (`neighbors() -> Vec<Neighbor>`) grew a heavyweight field (`peer_bloom`, added for the DEDUPLICATION.md Bloom exchange) after the routing consumer was written.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Phone with 20 neighbors in a shelter, 50 messages/s falling through to flood: 20 × 175 KB × 50 = 175 MB/s of allocation + copy, sustained. Allocator pressure, GC-like pauses, measurable battery drain.
- **Impact:** Severe CPU/allocator/battery cost per routing decision; lock hold time scales with neighbor Bloom size.
- **Fix:** Add a projection to `NeighborTable`, e.g. `pub async fn linked_up_ids(&self) -> Vec<PeerId>` (or `neighbor_summaries()` returning `(PeerId, NeighborState)`), and use it in `recipients_for_flood`. No clone of `peer_bloom` or `capabilities` should ever occur on the routing hot path.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `discovery/neighbor_table.rs:227-229` (new method; existing `neighbors()` callers unaffected), `gateway/mod.rs:679` has the same pattern and should be audited.

#### ROUT-21: `ForwardingDecision` carries no transport; neither Direct nor Flood verifies a usable transport exists
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `5ffffb0`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/mod.rs:62-75`; `crates/iris-core/src/routing/direct.rs:9-21`; `crates/iris-core/src/routing/flood.rs:52-56`
- **What:** The spec's `ForwardingDecision` is `{ next_hop, transport, delivery_probability, estimated_latency_ms, confidence }` and both Algorithm 1 and Algorithm 3 *select* a transport (`max_by_key(link_quality_score)` / `max_by_key(bandwidth_bps)`). The implementation's decision has only `next_hop` + `algorithm`. `try_direct` checks `is_up` (state == LinkedUp) and nothing else. In `recipients_for_flood` the transport check is a literal no-op block, and `has_live_transport` (`flood.rs:77-80`) is `#[allow(dead_code)]` and hard-coded `true`.
- **Evidence:**
```
flood.rs:52	        let nb = neighbor;
flood.rs:53	        if !nb.links.is_empty() {
flood.rs:54	            // Only neighbors with a live link qualify.
flood.rs:55	            let _ = &nb.links;
flood.rs:56	        }
```
```
flood.rs:77	#[allow(dead_code)]
flood.rs:78	fn has_live_transport(_transport: &TransportId) -> bool {
flood.rs:79	    true // reachability is enforced by the neighbor table state itself
flood.rs:80	}
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `BASELINE_ROUTING.md:37-41` and `:129-131`. Also `NeighborTable::transports_to` exists specifically *"(used by ROUTE-001 for multi-path selection)"* (`neighbor_table.rs:197-198`) and has no caller in `routing/`. `MULTIPATH_ROUTING.md` presumes a transport dimension in the decision.
- **Root cause:** The transport-selection half of Algorithms 1 and 3 was deferred; the placeholder block and dead helper were left in place so the code *reads* as if the check happens.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A peer is reachable only over a LoRa link that is duty-cycle-blocked, or only over a transport the local node has disabled. `is_up` is true (state is LinkedUp), so `try_direct` returns `Forward { next_hop }`. The caller has no transport to pick and must re-derive it, or picks the wrong one; on a duty-cycle-exhausted LoRa link the message silently stalls instead of falling through to Flood/Store.
- **Impact:** Message loss / stalling on multi-transport nodes; no quality- or bandwidth-based transport selection; the `if !nb.links.is_empty()` block gives a false impression of a liveness check during review.
- **Fix:** Add `transport: TransportId` to `ForwardingDecision::Forward` and `Flood`; use `NeighborTable::transports_to` + `LinkRecord::quality` to select; delete `has_live_transport` and the no-op block.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `ForwardingDecision` is public API (`lib.rs` re-export) → `tests/obs_telemetry.rs`, `sim/mod.rs`, all routing tests, any FFI consumer.

#### ROUT-22: `OpportunisticRouter::spray` has no memory of which contacts already hold a copy
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `eba51b6`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/opportunistic.rs:212-220` (fn `spray`)
- **What:** `spray` halves the budget for whatever `contact` it is handed, with no record of prior recipients. Calling it repeatedly with the *same* peer burns the copy budget on one node.
- **Evidence:**
```
212	    pub fn spray(&mut self, contact: &PeerId, budget: &mut SprayBudget) -> OpportunisticDecision {
213	        match budget.handoff() {
214	            Some(_) => OpportunisticDecision::ForwardTo {
215	                next_hop: *contact,
216	                reason: OpportunisticReason::Spray,
217	            },
218	            None => OpportunisticDecision::NoAdvantage,
219	        }
220	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `OPPORTUNISTIC_ROUTING.md:77` — *"**Spray phase**: distribute exactly L copies of the message to L **different** nodes"*. Binary spray's delivery guarantee depends on copy diversity; concentrating copies on one node is equivalent to L=1.
- **Root cause:** The router holds `max_dp_seen` for the PRoPHET path but no equivalent handed-to set for the spray path (`ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:86-87` says the router should hold the `SprayBudget` itself; it takes it as an out-parameter instead).
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Two nodes A and B in intermittent contact; the link flaps 3 times. A calls `spray(&B, &mut budget)` on each contact: 8→4 (give 4), 4→2 (give 2), 2→1 (give 1). B now holds 7 of the 8 copies and A is in wait phase. If B is a dead end, the message is lost despite L=8.
- **Impact:** Spray-and-wait degrades to single-copy; the L=8 delivery-rate claim in `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:64` does not hold. The test `spray_handoff_until_budget_exhausted` (`opportunistic.rs:329-347`) uses three *distinct* contacts and so cannot catch it.
- **Fix:** Track `sprayed_to: HashSet<(MessageId, PeerId)>` inside the router (or per `SprayBudget`) and return `NoAdvantage` for a repeat contact.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/mod.rs:509-517` implements its own spray bookkeeping and would need reconciling; `ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md` criterion 4.

#### ROUT-23: Spray L values contradict both spec tables; `DEFAULT_SPRAY_L = 8` is unreachable
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** 🔒 Blocked  ·  Tier 2  ·  reason: re-reading both governing specs during this fix confirms they **disagree with each other**, not just with the code — `OPPORTUNISTIC_ROUTING.md:125-131` gives P1=5, P2=3, P3=2 while `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:66-68` gives P1=L(=8), P2=L(=8), P3=max(4,…); only the P4+ ("1, direct-only") row is consistent between the two. There is no single spec to align the code to for P1-P3, and unilaterally picking one (or inventing a third value) risks a real delivery-behavior regression across every P1-P4 sim/production path — this is exactly the "wrong fix is worse than the original bug" case the loop's gate exists for. Needs a routing/product owner to reconcile the two specs (or affirm the current code as the intended policy and update both docs to match) before a code fix can be written with confidence. The narrower, policy-free half of the *Fix* field (decoupling the copy-cap dimension from the hop-cap dimension so `DEFAULT_SPRAY_L` is reachable at all) was deferred rather than fixed in isolation, since doing so without also resolving the P1-P3 value would still leave the effective L values undocumented/unjustified.  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/opportunistic.rs:25, 70-80` (const `DEFAULT_SPRAY_L`, fn `l_for_priority`)
- **What:** Two divergences. (a) P4/P5/P6 return 3 copies where both spec tables say 1 (direct-only). (b) The trailing `.min(hop_budget.max(1) as u32)` clamps L to the *hop* budget, which is 5 for P1/P2 and 3 for P4+ — so `DEFAULT_SPRAY_L = 8` can never be the effective value for any priority: P1/P2 → 5, P3 → 4, P4–P6 → 3, P7 → 1.
- **Evidence:**
```
70	    pub fn l_for_priority(p: MessagePriority, hop_budget: u8) -> u32 {
71	        match p {
72	            MessagePriority::P0 => return u32::MAX, // epidemic semantics
73	            MessagePriority::P1 | MessagePriority::P2 => DEFAULT_SPRAY_L,
74	            MessagePriority::P3 => 4,
75	            MessagePriority::P4 | MessagePriority::P5 | MessagePriority::P6 => 3,
76	            MessagePriority::P7 => 1,
77	        }
78	        .min(hop_budget.max(1) as u32)
79	        .max(1)
80	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `OPPORTUNISTIC_ROUTING.md:125-131` — P1=5, P2=3, P3=2, **P4+ = 1 (direct only)**. `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:66-68` — *"P1 = L, P2 = L, P3 = max(4, …), **P4+ = 1 (direct-only)**"*. `opportunistic.rs:25` cites *"EXP-ROUTE-002 validated"* for L=8, but 8 is never produced, so the validated parameter is not the shipped one. The code comment at lines 66-69 acknowledges the P4+ deviation but no doc was updated.
- **Root cause:** A deliberate local override ("direct-only would strand the store-carry class") that was never reflected back into either spec, plus a copy-count/hop-count dimension conflation.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Every P4–P6 message (the bulk traffic class) generates 3× the copies the design and the overhead budget assume. `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:114` claims *"Bounded overhead (no duplicate explosion) → spray cap L=8"*; the actual bulk-class cap is 3 where the spec says 1 — a 3× overhead regression on the highest-volume class.
- **Impact:** 3× airtime/battery overhead for bulk traffic vs. the documented design; the L=8 experimental validation does not apply to shipped behaviour.
- **Fix:** Decide and document one policy. If P4+ must be >1, amend `OPPORTUNISTIC_ROUTING.md:131` and `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:67` with the rationale; separate the copy cap from the hop cap so `DEFAULT_SPRAY_L` is reachable, or delete the constant.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/mod.rs:509`, `tests/sim_scenarios.rs:222`, `opportunistic.rs:234-246` tests, both spec tables.

#### ROUT-25: `OpportunisticRouter::spray` is never called by the engine — cold-start fallback is unimplemented
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `5ffffb0`  ·  2026-08-27 — implemented without ROUT-24 (candidate DP sourcing is not needed for spray, only a live contact is; see ROUT-24's blocked reason for why they were separable despite the stated Dependencies)
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/opportunistic.rs:212-220`; `crates/iris-core/src/routing/mod.rs:277-295`
- **What:** `decide_opportunistic` only calls `opp.decide(...)`. `spray()` has no caller anywhere in `crates/` outside `opportunistic.rs`'s own test at line 339 (`sim/mod.rs:509-517` reimplements spray using `SprayBudget` directly and never calls `router.spray`). `OpportunisticReason::Spray` is therefore never produced by the engine, and `RoutingEngine` holds no `SprayBudget` state.
- **Evidence:**
```
289	        match opp.decide(&recipient, candidates, priority, budget) {
290	            crate::routing::opportunistic::OpportunisticDecision::ForwardTo {
291	                next_hop, ..
292	            } => Some(next_hop),
293	            crate::routing::opportunistic::OpportunisticDecision::NoAdvantage => None,
294	        }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:21-23` — *"When the routing table has no useful history, L2 falls back to L0 binary spray-and-wait"*; `:86-87` says the router holds *"`DeliveryPredictability` + per-message `max_dp_seen` + `SprayBudget`"*; `:88-89` says `decide` returns a `SprayHandoff` variant. `OpportunisticDecision` (lines 41-49) has no `SprayHandoff` variant at all.

#### ROUT-26: `ForwardedCache`'s Bloom is ~351 KB — 5.5× the mandated 64 KB cap
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** 🔒 Blocked  ·  Tier 2  ·  reason: the *Fix* field itself concludes `REQ-ROUTE-NF-004`'s own numbers are internally inconsistent (64 KB cannot hold 400k ids at <1% FPR — that needs ~460 KB) and explicitly says "escalate to the requirements owner" rather than pick a resolution unilaterally. Needs a requirements-owner decision among: raise the cap to ~470 KB, lower capacity to ~55,000 ids at 1% FPR (64 KB), or accept a higher FPR. Not picked by the fix loop.  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/dedup_cache.rs:22, 36`
- **What:** `BloomFilter::new(200_000, 0.001)` → `bloom_bits` (`dedup.rs:34-38`) = `−200000·ln(0.001)/ln(2)²` ≈ 2,875,520 bits = **359,440 bytes ≈ 351 KB**, allocated eagerly in `Default` (so every `RoutingEngine::new()` costs 351 KB up front) — and, per ROUT-10, it contributes nothing to correctness.
- **Evidence:**
```
22	const WINDOW_CAPACITY: usize = 200_000;
...
36	            bloom: BloomFilter::new(WINDOW_CAPACITY, BLOOM_FPR),
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `ROUTING_REQUIREMENTS.md:92` — *"REQ-ROUTE-NF-004: The Bloom filter for deduplication **MUST** be bounded at 64 KB, providing < 1 % false positive rate for 400,000 bundle IDs (k=7 hash functions, m=512,000 bits)."* The delivered filter is 2,875,520 bits for 200,000 ids — 5.6× the mandated size *and* half the mandated capacity. (`BASELINE_ROUTING.md` §Resource Budget's looser "~500 KB" figure conflicts with the normative MUST; the requirement doc governs.)
- **Root cause:** The FPR was taken from `BASELINE_ROUTING.md`'s 0.1 % narrative rather than `REQ-ROUTE-NF-004`'s 1 %/64 KB/400 k parameters, and the capacity was halved.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Static: every node allocates 351 KB it does not need, on a platform budgeted at 512 MB total with `<5 MB` for all of Layer 0.
- **Impact:** Requirement violation; 5.6× RAM overspend on the dedup structure.
- **Fix:** `BloomFilter::new(400_000, 0.01)` → m ≈ 3.83 Mbit… still over. To hit the spec's m=512,000 bits at n=400,000 the FPR is ~0.28 per the standard formula, so **REQ-ROUTE-NF-004's own numbers are internally inconsistent** (64 KB cannot hold 400 k ids at <1 % FPR — that needs ~460 KB). Escalate to the requirements owner: either raise the cap to ~470 KB, lower the capacity to ~55,000 ids at 1 % FPR (64 KB), or accept a higher FPR. Do not silently ship 351 KB against a 64 KB MUST.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `ROUTING_REQUIREMENTS.md:92`, `BASELINE_ROUTING.md` §Resource Budget, `message_engine/dedup.rs` (`BLOOM_CAPACITY` uses the same formula and should be checked against the same requirement).

```
207	                "flood must respect hop budget (got {hop} > {max})"
208	            );
209	            // Termination is guaranteed by the visited set; no node revisited.
210	            assert_eq!(
211	                visited.len(),
212	                visited.len(),
213	                "visited set is a set by construction"
214	            );
215	            // Every frontier round strictly increases hop count — monotonic.
216	            let _ = reached;
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `ROUTE_VERIFICATION.md:38` cites this test as the ✅ PASS evidence for criterion 2 (*"Flood terminates; no loops; hop-count monotonic"*), and `ROUTE2_DESIGN.md` / ORCH-0001 WP-4 acceptance depends on it. The test would still pass if `recipients_for_flood` returned the sender, returned every peer including already-flooded ones, or returned an empty vec.
- **Root cause:** A property test written around a simulation harness that was never given a real topology; assertions were softened to whatever passed.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Invert the `nb.peer_id == sender` guard at `flood.rs:57` to `!=` — the test still passes. That is the definition of no coverage.
- **Impact:** The single most important correctness property of Algorithm 3 is unverified while being reported as verified. ROUT-4, ROUT-9 and ROUT-17 all live in code this test nominally covers.
- **Fix:** Model the topology as `HashMap<PeerId, NeighborTable>` (one table per node) built from a seeded RNG; assert (a) `visited` never grows after the hop cap, (b) `reached` is true whenever a path of length ≤ cap exists, (c) no node appears in two frontiers, (d) total transmissions ≤ an explicit fan-out bound. Use a seeded RNG (`StdRng::seed_from_u64`) for reproducibility rather than `thread_rng`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `ROUTE_VERIFICATION.md:38` must be downgraded until the test is real; the rewritten test will fail against current code (ROUT-4, ROUT-17), which is the point.

#### ROUT-29: `flood_no_backtrack_no_reflood_property` builds a nonsensical already-flooded set, making its assertions near-vacuous
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `7d5723d`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/flood.rs:220-245` (test `flood_no_backtrack_no_reflood_property`)
- **What:** The `already` set is `(1..=8).filter(|i| *i != sender.0[0] % 8).map(|i| pid(i + 1))` — the filter compares a 1-based index against `sender_id % 8` (which is 0 when the sender is `pid(8)`, so nothing is ever filtered for that case), and the `+1` shifts the result to `pid(2)..=pid(9)`, where `pid(9)` is not in the table at all. Net effect: `already` contains 7–8 of the table's 8 peers, so `recipients_for_flood` returns at most `[pid(1)]` (or nothing when the sender is `pid(1)`). The two assertions then hold trivially against an almost-empty result.
- **Evidence:**
```
233	            let sender = pid(rng.gen_range(1..=8));
234	            let already: Vec<PeerId> = (1..=8u8)
235	                .filter(|i| *i != sender.0[0] % 8)
236	                .map(|i| pid(i + 1))
237	                .collect();
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `ROUTE_VERIFICATION.md:38` cites this as evidence for the no-backtrack/no-reflood property. Asserting that a 0–1 element result excludes 8 specific peers proves nothing about the exclusion logic.
- **Root cause:** Two independent index-arithmetic slips (`% 8` on a 1-based range; `pid(i + 1)` instead of `pid(i)`) that happen to make the test pass.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Remove the `already_flooded.contains(&nb.peer_id)` term from `flood.rs:59` entirely — the assertion loop then fails, so this one is not *fully* vacuous. But remove the `nb.peer_id == sender` term and the test still passes for every seed where `sender` is in `already` (7 of 8 cases), which it is by construction.
- **Impact:** Weak coverage on the no-backtrack invariant; reported as verified.
- **Fix:** Build `already` as an explicit, meaningful subset (e.g. `vec![pid(3), pid(5)]`), assert the *exact* expected recipient set, and cover the empty-`already` case so the sender exclusion is independently exercised.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `ROUTE_VERIFICATION.md:38`.

#### ROUT-31: `ttl_check_arrival_time` enshrines the immortality bug, and `>` vs `<=` puts `store::is_expired` one second out of step with `expiry::is_expired`
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed (subsumed by ROUT-5)  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `1821c48`  ·  verified still current 2026-08-27 — re-read `store.rs` at HEAD: `is_expired` is now a thin shim delegating to `message_engine::expiry::is_expired` (the `<=` boundary), and `ttl_check_arrival_time`'s third assertion now documents skew-budget tolerance (100s future, within 300s budget → not expired) rather than the original unconditional-immortality bug; `rout5_far_future_timestamp_fails_closed` covers the fail-closed case beyond the skew budget. No further code change needed here — see ROUT-36 (still open) for the remaining same-name/different-argument-order hazard between the two functions.
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/store.rs:33, 68-76` (fn `is_expired`, test `ttl_check_arrival_time`)
- **What:** Two problems. (a) The test's third assertion — `assert!(!is_expired(100, 200, 60));` under the comment *"timestamp in the future (skew) never counts against earlier"* — is the ROUT-5 vulnerability written down as intended behaviour, which is why ROUT-5 survived. (b) `store::is_expired` uses `elapsed > ttl_seconds` while `message_engine::expiry::is_expired` uses `expiry <= now_unix` (i.e. `elapsed >= ttl`). The two disagree at exactly `elapsed == ttl_seconds`.
- **Evidence:**
```
33	    now_unix.saturating_sub(lifetime_start) > ttl_seconds
```
```
71	        assert!(is_expired(120, 0, 60));
72	        // still within budget.
73	        assert!(!is_expired(59, 0, 60));
74	        // timestamp in the future (skew) never counts against earlier.
75	        assert!(!is_expired(100, 200, 60));
```
  vs `expiry.rs:160-162` — `assert!(is_expired(NOW - 300, 300, NOW));` (expired at exactly ttl).
- **Why it is wrong:** `store.rs:29-30` claims the function is *"Exposed here so the routing layer and the store share one definition"* — but there are two definitions with different boundary semantics and opposite skew handling. A message can be simultaneously "expired" to the message engine and "live" to SCF.
- **Root cause:** Independent implementations of the same predicate; the message-engine one was later hardened (`expiry.rs:55-64`) without touching this one, and this one's test locked in the old behaviour.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `now = 1000, timestamp = 700, ttl = 300`. `expiry::is_expired(700, 300, 1000)` → true (dropped by the engine). `store::is_expired(1000, 700, 300)` → `300 > 300` → false (SCF keeps carrying it). SCF forwards a message the engine will drop on arrival — wasted airtime on every contact for the message's remaining life.
- **Impact:** Inconsistent expiry across layers; the test actively blocks the ROUT-5 fix.
- **Fix:** Delete `store::is_expired` and re-export the `message_engine::expiry` version (ROUT-5). Replace `ttl_check_arrival_time` with assertions matching `expiry.rs:180-197` — including `assert!(is_expired(NOW, NOW + 1_000_000_000, 300))`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** ROUT-5; `scf.rs:207, 267, 307`; note the two functions also have **swapped argument orders** (`(now, timestamp, ttl)` vs `(created, ttl, now)`) — unifying them is a mechanical but error-prone change that must be reviewed call-site by call-site.

```
28	        e.clear();
...

```
  (`e.clear()` at line 28 and `snapshot.clear()` at line 45 are both no-ops on values about to be dropped.)
- **Why it is wrong:** `BASELINE_ROUTING.md` §Resource Budget sets explicit per-algorithm latency/CPU targets (Algorithm 1 <1 µs, Algorithm 2 <10 µs, Algorithm 3 <1 ms for 10 neighbors, dedup check <0.5 µs, full decision <10 ms). # R1 — Deep bug hunt: DTN / store-carry-forward / PRoPHET
Scope: `crates/iris-core/src/routing/{prophet,scf,scf_contact,scf_eviction}.rs`

#### DTN-1: SCF store is completely unbounded — `buffer_message` never enforces `max_bytes` and eviction is never called in production
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:199-226` (fn `buffer_message`); callers proven by grep
- **What:** `buffer_message` checks TTL only. It never compares `self.usage()` against `self.max_bytes`, never calls `evict_to_fit`/`evict_until`, and never returns a "storage full" error. `DropReason::StorageFull` (scf.rs:40) is never constructed.
- **Evidence:**
```
207	        if is_expired(self.now_unix(), envelope.timestamp, envelope.ttl_seconds) {
208	            return Err(ScfError::Expired);
209	        }
210	        let key = StoreKey::from_envelope(&envelope);
218	        self.buffer.insert(key, stored);
225	        Ok(DeliveryStatus::Stored)
```
  Repo-wide grep `evict_to_fit|evict_to_capacity|evict_until` over `crates/ --include=*.rs`:
  `crates/iris-core/src/routing/mod.rs:579` (inside `#[cfg(test)]`) and `crates/iris-core/tests/obs_telemetry.rs:124` (test). **Zero production call sites.** `evict_to_capacity` and `evict_until` have no callers at all outside the module.
- **Why it is wrong:** STORE_CARRY_FORWARD.md §Storage Capacity mandates a hard `max_bytes` (default 500 MB; 200 MB phone) and §Eviction Policy states that when space cannot be freed the node drops the incoming message. `ScfConfig::max_storage_bytes` is copied into `self.max_bytes` (scf.rs:124) and read *only* by `evict_to_fit`, which nothing calls.
- **Root cause:** The comment at scf.rs:200-201 ("buffer size is capped by `max_bytes` (eviction enforced separately via `evict_to_fit`)") pushed enforcement onto a caller that was never written.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Long-lived partition. A phone keeps receiving relayed envelopes (`crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:388` calls `buffer_message` per hop). Nothing sweeps either: `reap_expired` also has **zero production callers** (grep: only scf.rs:302 definition and scf.rs:510 test). The `BTreeMap` grows until OOM-kill.
- **Impact:** Remote, unauthenticated OOM DoS on every relay node; total loss of all buffered P0/SOS traffic when the process dies.
- **Fix:** Enforce inside `buffer_message`:
```rust
let need = Self::approx_bytes(&envelope);
if self.usage().saturating_add(need) > self.max_bytes {
    self.evict_until(self.max_bytes.saturating_sub(need));
    if self.usage().saturating_add(need) > self.max_bytes {
        return Err(ScfError::StorageFull);
    }
}
```
  and add a message-COUNT cap alongside the byte cap. Schedule `reap_expired` on a timer (spec: hourly cleanup).
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `ScfError` is `PartialEq`-matched in tests (scf.rs:472); a new variant touches `routing/mod.rs:46` re-exports, `sim/mod.rs:388,574`, `obs_telemetry.rs`. Needs a new INV-ROUTE bound test.

#### DTN-2: No message-COUNT bound and no duplicate suppression — the same `MessageId` can occupy unlimited slots
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:56-71` (`StoreKey`), `scf.rs:210-218` (fn `buffer_message`)
- **What:** The buffer is keyed by `StoreKey { priority_rank, expiry_unix, message_id }`. `buffer_message` performs no lookup by `MessageId`. Two envelopes with the same `message_id` but a different `priority` or `timestamp`/`ttl_seconds` produce different `StoreKey`s and therefore two distinct buffer entries.
- **Evidence:**
```
64	    pub fn from_envelope(env: &Envelope) -> Self {
65	        StoreKey {
66	            priority_rank: env.priority.as_u8(),
67	            expiry_unix: env.timestamp.saturating_add(env.ttl_seconds),
68	            message_id: env.message_id,
69	        }
70	    }
218	        self.buffer.insert(key, stored);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Every by-id accessor (`priority_rank_of` scf.rs:163, `delivery_status` scf.rs:375, `mark_forwarded` scf.rs:286, `status_for` scf.rs:230) does `.iter().find(..)` and returns the **first** match in `StoreKey` order — so marking one copy Delivered leaves the other live and forwardable. There is also no `max_messages` knob in `ScfConfig` at all.
- **Root cause:** The design copied the spec's `BTreeMap<StoreKey, _>` ordering index but omitted the primary-key-by-`MessageId` map the spec's SQLite schema has (`id BLOB PRIMARY KEY`).
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A peer replays one envelope N times with `ttl_seconds` incremented by 1 each time (TTL is not covered by any signature check at this layer; `buffer_message` accepts `Envelope` with `signature: Option<_>` unverified). N buffer entries of the same payload. With tiny payloads each costs ~256 B accounted, so the entry count explodes long before any byte ceiling (which per DTN-1 does not exist).
- **Impact:** Amplified memory exhaustion; duplicate forwarding of the same message to the same peer; `delivery_status` reports the wrong copy's status.
- **Fix:** Add `index: HashMap<MessageId, StoreKey>`; in `buffer_message`, if the id is present, keep (or replace after removing the old key). Route all by-id accessors through the index (also removes the O(n) scans). Add `max_messages` to `ScfConfig`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** every `.iter().find` accessor in scf.rs; `routing/dedup_cache.rs` (a bounded dedup primitive that SCF never consults — see DTN-3).

#### DTN-3: No per-peer "already offered" record — the same message is re-offered to the same peer on every contact event
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `b58de3d`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf_contact.rs:64-97` (fn `on_new_contact`), `scf.rs:257-274` (`messages_forwardable_to`)
- **What:** `on_new_contact` re-derives the full candidate list from the buffer on every contact event. `ScfEngine` holds no `(message_id, peer)` "offered/sent" set. The only limiter is the **global** `forward_attempts < max_forward_attempts` counter (scf.rs:264), which is not per-peer.
- **Evidence:**
```
269	        let candidates = self.messages_forwardable_to(contact);
270	        let mut ranked: Vec<ForwardCandidate> = candidates
286	        ranked.sort_by_key(|c| self.message_priority(c));
```
  and the only repeat limiter:
```
264	            .filter(|(_, m)| m.forward_attempts < self.config.max_forward_attempts)
```
- **Why it is wrong:** In DTN, contact events for the same neighbor fire repeatedly (BLE advertise/disconnect/re-advertise is seconds-scale). The same message is re-offered every time. Conversely, because the counter is global, meeting three *different* peers exhausts the budget and the message becomes permanently unforwardable to everyone (see DTN-13).
- **Root cause:** History is only encoded in the mutable `DeliveryStatus` enum, which the next forward overwrites; nothing is retained.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Node A carries msg M for recipient R. A and R flap in and out of BLE range 3 times in 10 s: `on_new_contact` returns M each time; `forward_attempts` reaches 3; M is now permanently unforwardable even once a stable contact appears. R meanwhile received 3 copies.
- **Impact:** Bandwidth waste on scarce BLE/LoRa links; premature permanent lock-out of live messages.
- **Fix:** Add a bounded `offered: HashMap<MessageId, SmallSet<PeerId>>` filtered inside `messages_forwardable_to`, and make `forward_attempts` per-peer. Reuse the bounded-set primitive in `routing/dedup_cache.rs` rather than an unbounded `HashSet`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `scf_contact.rs`, `sim/mod.rs:388-402`, SCF_VERIFICATION.md acceptance criteria.

#### DTN-4: `messages_forwardable_to` requires an EXACT recipient match — multi-hop store-carry-forward relaying is impossible
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `b58de3d`  ·  2026-08-27  ·  scope note: fixed together with DTN-3 (its per-peer dedup is what makes opening relay eligibility to every live contact safe). Any live, not-yet-offered message is now a relay candidate for any contact — the module's core premise (relay actually happens) now works. The *Fix* field's suggested `oracle.is_better_carrier` DP-based selectivity was **not** implemented: it is blocked by the same gap as ROUT-24 (this tier, earlier) — no wire protocol in this crate exchanges a live contact's own delivery-predictability data, so "is contact a better carrier than me" cannot be computed from data that exists. Exact-recipient match keeps its higher-confidence ranking (0.9 vs 0.6) so the module isn't blind to the distinction, just not yet DP-optimized.
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:257-276` (fn `messages_forwardable_to`)
- **What:** The doc comment promises "those addressed to it **or relayable toward it**". The code keeps only messages whose `recipient_id` equals the contact.
- **Evidence:**
```
257	    /// Messages forwardable to a contact: those addressed to it or relayable
258	    /// toward it, not yet terminal, within TTL and still under the forward
265	            .filter(|(_, m)| {
266	                let matches = Self::recipient_is(contact, &m.envelope);
267	                let live = !is_expired(
271	                );
272	                matches && live
273	            })
```
- **Why it is wrong:** This defeats the module's premise. STORE_CARRY_FORWARD.md §Core Concept: "Time 1: A stores message in B's buffer (**B is a relay candidate**)"; §Vehicle Relay Scenario has a volunteer's phone carrying 47 messages *none addressed to the volunteer*. Under this code a carrier meeting an intermediate peer forwards **nothing**.
- **Root cause:** `recipient_is` was the easy predicate; the "relayable toward it" half (PRoPHET DP consult / gateway hint) was never wired. `scf_contact.rs:56-57` even contains a dead branch commented "Relay candidate: still worth attempting, lower confidence" returning `0.6` — **unreachable**, because every candidate surviving `messages_forwardable_to` is by construction addressed to `contact`, so `delivery_probability` always returns `0.9`.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Field team A → medical post C via volunteer B. B buffers the message, drives to C's region, meets relay D that is one hop from C. `messages_forwardable_to(&D)` returns `[]`. The message sits in B until TTL.
- **Impact:** The DTN layer degrades to direct delivery only. In the canonical earthquake scenario, zero messages are delivered. Renders the `0.6` relay probability, the entire `delivery_probability` ranking, and PRoPHET's DP table pointless at the SCF layer.
- **Fix:** Extend the filter to `recipient_is(contact, env) || oracle.is_better_carrier(contact, recipient_of(env))`, threading `OpportunisticRouter`/`DeliveryPredictability` (or a `&dyn ForwardOracle`) into `ScfEngine`. Keep exact-match at 0.9 and the DP-derived case at the actual DP.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `scf_contact.rs::delivery_probability`, `routing/opportunistic.rs`, the `sim/mod.rs` relay path, SCF_VERIFICATION.md, and the tests `forwardable_to_contact_only` (scf.rs:477) and `contact_ranks_p0_first_then_probability` (scf_contact.rs:164), which currently lock in the broken behaviour.

#### DTN-5: Delivered / Dropped messages are never removed from the buffer — terminal entries leak forever
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:278-299` (fn `mark_forwarded`), `scf.rs:44-51`
- **What:** `mark_forwarded(.., acked = true)` sets `DeliveryStatus::Delivered` in place. Nothing removes the entry. The only removal paths are `reap_expired` (TTL; no production caller, DTN-1) and `evict_until` (no production caller, DTN-1).
- **Evidence:**
```
291	        let msg = self.buffer.get_mut(&key)?;
292	        msg.forward_attempts += 1;
293	        msg.delivery_status = if acked {
294	            DeliveryStatus::Delivered { delivered_to: to }
295	        } else {
296	            DeliveryStatus::AckPending { sent_to: to }
297	        };
```
- **Why it is wrong:** STORE_CARRY_FORWARD.md §Message Lifecycle: "ACK_RECEIVED → DELIVERED → **(remove from store)**" and "TTL_EXPIRED → DROPPED → (remove from store, log)". A delivered message still occupies bytes counted by `usage()` (scf.rs:170-175), inflating capacity accounting and (once DTN-1 is fixed) causing live messages to be evicted in its favour.
- **Root cause:** Status modelled as mutable state on a retained record instead of as a removal event.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `sim/mod.rs:390-396` buffers a copy at the destination and immediately `mark_forwarded(.., true)` on it. That entry is terminal and immortal. Delivered messages accumulate their full payloads in RAM until TTL — and with an attacker-chosen far-future `timestamp` (DTN-6), TTL never elapses.
- **Impact:** Unbounded RAM growth proportional to lifetime delivered traffic; the primary OOM vector on a *healthy* (non-partitioned) node.
- **Fix:** In `mark_forwarded`, on `acked == true`, remove the entry and return the terminal status by value.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** scf.rs test `buffer_and_lifecycle_status` (line 448) asserts `delivery_status(&id) == Some(Delivered{..})` *after* the ack — that assertion must invert. Same for `routing/mod.rs:568-576` and `sim/mod.rs:393-395`.

#### DTN-6: `expiry_unix` and the TTL check trust an attacker-controlled `timestamp`/`ttl_seconds` — messages can be made unexpirable and eviction-proof
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:63-70` (`StoreKey::from_envelope`), `crates/iris-core/src/routing/store.rs:31-34` (fn `is_expired`), `scf.rs:337-351` (`evict_until` ordering)
- **What:** `is_expired` clamps the lifetime start to `timestamp.min(now_unix)` — a *future* timestamp is treated as "arrived now", so the message survives until `ttl_seconds` elapses from now. `ttl_seconds` is never clamped. Simultaneously `StoreKey::expiry_unix = timestamp + ttl_seconds` is taken at face value, and `evict_until` treats a *later* `expiry_unix` as safer.
- **Evidence:**
```
store.rs:31	pub fn is_expired(now_unix: u64, timestamp: u64, ttl_seconds: u64) -> bool {
store.rs:32	    let lifetime_start = timestamp.min(now_unix);
store.rs:33	    now_unix.saturating_sub(lifetime_start) > ttl_seconds
store.rs:34	}
scf.rs:67	            expiry_unix: env.timestamp.saturating_add(env.ttl_seconds),
scf.rs:349	                        .then_with(|| b.expiry_unix.cmp(&a.expiry_unix)) // sooner expiry = worse
```
- **Why it is wrong:** (a) `ttl_seconds = u64::MAX` makes `is_expired` permanently false, so `reap_expired` can never drop the message. (b) The eviction comparator ranks by the *claimed* `expiry_unix`, which the sender inflates for free — attacker traffic is always the last evicted within its band while honest soon-expiring traffic goes first.
- **Root cause:** `ScfConfig::clock_skew_budget_secs` (scf.rs:103-104, default 300) was added exactly to bound this and is **never read** — grep across `crates/` returns only scf.rs (declaration + default) and an unrelated `message_engine/mod.rs:84,100`. Unwired knob.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A peer sends 1000 P1 envelopes with `timestamp = now + 10 years, ttl_seconds = u64::MAX`. They never expire and sort as the highest `expiry_unix` in P1, so every honest P1..P7 message is evicted around them.
- **Impact:** Permanent store poisoning; guaranteed eviction of legitimate traffic; TTL sweep neutralised.
- **Fix:** In `buffer_message`, reject/clamp: `if envelope.timestamp > now + self.config.clock_skew_budget_secs { return Err(ScfError::ClockSkew) }` and `let ttl = envelope.ttl_seconds.min(MAX_TTL_SECS)`. Base `StoreKey::expiry_unix` on `stored_at + ttl` (locally observed arrival), not on the claimed `timestamp` — exactly the RFC 9171 §4.4.2 arrival-time semantics the code comment already cites.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/store.rs::is_expired` is shared with the store layer; the key-derivation change is local to `StoreKey::from_envelope`. Skew rejection needs a new `ScfError` variant (DTN-1). Re-verify `reap_expired`, `evict_until`, and store.rs test `ttl_check_arrival_time` (line 69), which currently *asserts* the future-timestamp leniency.

#### DTN-7: `evict_until` silently gives up when only P0 remains — a P0/SOS flood is an unbounded, uncapped memory sink
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27  ·  scope note: fixed via DTN-1's reject-on-insert enforcement (buffer_message rejects any message, P0 included, once evict_until has nothing left it may evict and the ceiling would still be exceeded) — this alone bounds usage() at max_bytes regardless of priority mix, which is the finding's core "unbounded" defect. The *Fix* field's secondary suggestion (a dedicated 25%-of-max_bytes P0 sub-quota with its own oldest-first eviction) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is a refinement for P0-vs-other-traffic fairness, not required to close the unbounded-growth defect, and would have needed new config surface + a P0-internal eviction ordering (by `stored_at`, distinct from the existing expiry-based comparator) without a clear specified default. Left as a possible follow-up, not a gap in this fix.
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:337-366` (fn `evict_until`)
- **What:** The loop filters `k.priority_rank > 0` (P0 exempt). When every remaining message is P0, `max_by` yields `None` and the loop `break`s, leaving usage arbitrarily above `target_bytes` and returning a short/empty eviction list. No caller is told the target was not met.
- **Evidence:**
```
339	        while self.usage() > target_bytes {
345	                .filter(|(k, _)| k.priority_rank > 0) // P0 exempt
352	            let Some(k) = worst else { break };
365	        evicted
```
- **Why it is wrong:** INV-ROUTE-003 ("P0 never evicted") and the capacity bound conflict, and the code resolves it by abandoning the bound with no signal. STORE_CARRY_FORWARD.md §Eviction Policy resolves it the other way — it breaks *and* drops the **incoming** message ("Store full, cannot evict P0; dropping incoming message"). The code has no incoming-drop path at all (DTN-1), so nothing stops growth.
- **Root cause:** `evict_until` returns `Vec<MessageId>` with no success/failure discriminant, so "gave up" is unrepresentable.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A node receives P0 traffic only. `usage()` climbs past 500 MB, past 2 GB, until OOM. `MessagePriority::P0` is a plain envelope field with no authorisation check in this module — any peer can set it.
- **Impact:** The most safety-critical message class is also the unbounded one; the node dies exactly when P0 traffic matters most, losing every buffered P0 message.
- **Fix:** Return `(Vec<MessageId>, bool /*target_met*/)` or an `EvictOutcome`; on failure have `buffer_message` reject the incoming message per spec. Additionally give P0 its own sub-quota (e.g. 25 % of `max_bytes`) with oldest-first eviction *within* that quota — pure exemption is not implementable under a hard memory limit.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `evict_to_fit`, `evict_to_capacity`, `scf_eviction.rs` tests `p0_never_evicted_under_pressure` (line 137) and `device_class_ceiling_trims_to_class` (line 188), INV-ROUTE-003 in ROUTING_REQUIREMENTS.md, SCF_VERIFICATION.md.

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:170-175` (fn `usage`), `scf.rs:339,346-351,359`
- **What:** `usage()` sums `approx_bytes` over the whole `BTreeMap` on every call. `evict_until` calls it in the `while` condition *and* again inside the `tracing::warn!` field list, and separately rescans the map with `max_by` for each victim. Evicting `m` of `n` costs O(m·n).
- **Evidence:**
```

171	        self.buffer
172	            .values()
173	            .map(|m| Self::approx_bytes(&m.envelope))
174	            .sum()
175	    }
339	        while self.usage() > target_bytes {
346	                .max_by(|(a, _), (b, _)| {
359	                    usage_bytes = self.usage(),
```
- **Why it is wrong:** STORE_CARRY_FORWARD.md's data model carries an incrementally maintained `total_bytes` field precisely to make this O(1); the implementation dropped it. Eviction is a `warn`-level event, so the line-359 `usage()` is evaluated on every iteration at default log levels.
- **Root cause:** Recomputation was chosen to avoid accounting drift, at the cost of complexity.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** 500 MB filled with 1 KB messages ≈ 500 000 entries. Freeing 10 % (50 000 evictions) is ~2.5 × 10^10 traversal steps plus 50 000 full `max_by` scans. The engine stalls for minutes on a phone, blocking the routing task.

- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `usage_bytes()` (scf.rs:158), `sim/metrics.rs:70`, `sim/mod.rs:284`, `scf_eviction.rs::evict_to_capacity`.

#### DTN-9: The `BTreeMap` key ordering does not match the eviction order the spec and doc comments claim
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:53-61` (`StoreKey`), `scf.rs:368-372` (`ordered_buffered`), `scf.rs:337-351`
- **What:** `StoreKey` derives `Ord` as (`priority_rank` ASC, `expiry_unix` ASC, `message_id`). scf.rs:5-6 and 368-369 describe the map as "priority DESC, expiry ASC", and the spec's eviction takes `keys().next_back()` as "lowest priority, soonest expiry". With this `Ord`, `next_back()` is lowest priority, **LATEST** expiry — the opposite tie-break. `evict_until` therefore cannot use map order at all and falls back to a full `max_by` scan with a hand-inverted comparator (scf.rs:346-350).
- **Evidence:**
```
56	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
57	pub struct StoreKey {
58	    pub priority_rank: u8, // 0 = P0, 7 = P7
59	    pub expiry_unix: u64,  // sooner expiry = smaller
368	    /// All buffered messages ordered (priority DESC, expiry ASC) — the
369	    /// forward order the contact handler uses.
370	    pub fn ordered_buffered(&self) -> Vec<StoredMessage> {
371	        self.buffer.values().cloned().collect()
372	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Two representations of "the eviction order" now exist and disagree. The comment "priority DESC" is also plainly false — the map is priority-rank ASC (P0 first).
- **Root cause:** `#[derive(Ord)]` on a struct whose two ranking fields need opposite directions.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Not a runtime failure today (the `max_by` comparator is independently correct), but the obvious O(1) fix for DTN-8 — `next_back()` — silently inverts the expiry tie-break, evicting the *latest*-expiring message in the lowest band instead of the soonest.
- **Impact:** Latent policy inversion; misleading doc comments across four sites.
- **Fix:** Store expiry as `Reverse(u64)` (or `u64::MAX - expiry`) so the derived `Ord` genuinely puts the worst victim last, then replace `max_by` with `next_back()`. Correct the `ordered_buffered` comment.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** scf.rs test `store_key_ordering_priority_then_expiry` (line 517) only checks the priority axis and one same-priority pair — it must be extended. `sim/mod.rs:600-601` consumes `ordered_buffered` ordering.

#### DTN-10: `approx_bytes` counts only the payload — attacker-controlled envelope fields (cert chain, routing hints, encryption header) are invisible to capacity accounting
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `c0c1007`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:187-189` (fn `approx_bytes`)
- **What:** Accounting is `payload.len() + 256`, a flat constant for everything else. `Envelope` also carries `payload_ref`, `signature`, `encryption_hdr`, `routing_hints`, `auth_cert_chain` (see `crates/iris-core/src/protocol/envelope.rs` and the literal at `scf_eviction.rs:102-107`) — all heap-allocated, none counted.
- **Evidence:**
```
187	    fn approx_bytes(env: &Envelope) -> u64 {
188	        env.payload.len() as u64 + 256
189	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The ceiling is meant to bound *resident memory*. Under-counting means the real footprint can exceed `max_bytes` by an unbounded factor while `usage()` reports the node as under budget, so eviction never fires (even once DTN-1 is fixed) and the `storage_bytes_used / storage_bytes_max` health indicator from STORE_CARRY_FORWARD.md §SCF Metrics reads healthy while the device is out of RAM.
- **Root cause:** "Approximate" was read as "payload-dominated", which holds for text but not for messages carrying certificate chains or multi-recipient encryption headers.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** 100 000 envelopes with a 1-byte payload and a 64 KB `auth_cert_chain`. Accounted usage ≈ 25 MB (well under 200 MB). Actual resident > 6 GB.
- **Impact:** The capacity bound is bypassable by construction; OOM despite a correctly implemented ceiling.
- **Fix:** Account the serialized size once at insert (`envelope.encoded_len()`) and cache it on `StoredMessage` — which also fixes DTN-8's recomputation cost.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `usage`, `usage_bytes`, `evict_until`, `scf_eviction.rs` `mk()` helper (line 111, assumes `bytes - 256` payload sizing), `sim/metrics.rs:70`.

- **Fix:** Have `ScfEngine::new` take a `DeviceClass` (or resolve it from platform config) and set `max_bytes = class.max_bytes().min(config.max_storage_bytes)`. Make `evict_until` call `ScfEvictionPolicy::is_evictable(..)` instead of the inline `priority_rank > 0`, and use `eviction_weight` as the comparator key. Fix the `eviction_weight` doc comment.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/mod.rs:46`; `scf.rs:120-129` constructor signature (called from `sim/mod.rs:58-62`, `routing/mod.rs:551`, `tests/obs_telemetry.rs`); SCF_VERIFICATION.md.

#### DTN-12: PRoPHET aging is never executed in production — `age()` and `prune()` have no non-benchmark callers, so DPs only ever increase
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `9b823e0`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:151-181` (fn `age`), `prophet.rs:258-273` (fn `prune`)
- **What:** RFC 6693 Eq. 2 (`P = P_old · gamma^K`) is implemented but never invoked by any production path.
- **Evidence:** Repo-wide grep `\.age\(\)|\.prune\(\)` over `crates/ --include=*.rs`, excluding prophet.rs: exactly one hit, `crates/iris-core/benches/routing.rs:49: b.iter(|| black_box(pred.age()))` — a Criterion benchmark. `prune()` has zero hits anywhere. `OpportunisticRouter` (opportunistic.rs:98-220) exposes `predictions_mut()` but never ages; `sim/mod.rs` only calls `on_contact`/`snapshot` (lines 424-425); `routing/mod.rs:177` only calls `meet`.
- **Why it is wrong:** ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:38 lists Eq. 2 as required, and ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:131 names aging as the mitigation for "Aging clock wrong / node churn — stale DPs decay via gamma^K". Without aging, the table is monotonically non-decreasing: Eq. 1 always increases toward `1 - delta` (prophet.rs:216) and Eq. 3 is a MAX that only increases (prophet.rs:232-236). Every DP the node ever learned stays at its historical peak forever.
- **Root cause:** No scheduler or routing tick owns the DP table; `age()` was written for a caller that never materialised — the same failure mode as `reap_expired` (DTN-1).
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Node A meets B once, learns `P(A,B) = 0.495` and transitively `P(A,C) = 0.4`. B is destroyed and never seen again. A month later A still reports `P(A,C) = 0.4`, and `gtmx_advantage` (opportunistic.rs:151-183) still selects carriers from it. Messages are steered toward a dead branch of the network.
- **Impact:** PRoPHET degenerates into flooding-with-stale-preferences; routing quality decays monotonically with uptime; also removes the only mechanism that would ever shrink the DP table (DTN-15).
- **Fix:** Call `age()` from the routing tick and, per RFC 6693 §2.1.2, immediately before every `snapshot()` and before any `p_for()` used in a forwarding decision. Fix the aging math first — see DTN-13.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `opportunistic.rs::on_contact`/`decide`, `routing/mod.rs:177`, `sim/mod.rs:424-425` (enabling aging changes simulation output, so `tests/ml_experiments.rs` anchors shift), ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md row 1.

#### DTN-13: `age()` resets `last_meet` to *now* for every entry — calling it more often than `aging_interval` means aging never happens at all
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `9b823e0`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:154-181` (fn `age`)
- **What:** For each surviving entry `age()` pushes `(dst, aged, now)` and rewrites `last_meet[dst] = now` — **unconditionally, including when `k == 0`**. The elapsed time that did not amount to a whole interval is discarded rather than carried forward.
- **Evidence:**
```
159	            let k = self
160	                .last_meet
161	                .get(dst)
162	                .map(|t| floor_intervals(now.saturating_sub(*t), cfg.aging_interval))
163	                .unwrap_or(0u64);
164	            let aged = if k > 0 {
165	                p * cfg.gamma.powi(k as i32)
166	            } else {
167	                *p
168	            };
169	            if aged >= cfg.p_first_threshold {
170	                aging.push((*dst, aged, now));
171	            }
176	        for (dst, aged, at) in aging {
177	            self.dps.insert(dst, aged);
178	            self.last_meet.insert(dst, at);
179	        }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `floor_intervals` is exact floor division — the Kani proof `prophet_floor_intervals_division` (`crates/iris-core/src/kani_proofs.rs:143-155`) asserts `k == elapsed_ns / interval_ns`. Floor division is only a correct aging step if the **remainder is preserved**. Setting the baseline to `now` discards the remainder on every call, so with an aging cadence shorter than `aging_interval` (30 min by default) `k` is 0 forever and `gamma` is never applied. A 60-second routing tick against the 1800-second default yields **exactly zero decay in perpetuity**.
- **Root cause:** "Last update time" and "last aging-baseline time" were conflated. Because `age()` is currently uncalled (DTN-12), the defect is invisible today.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Fix DTN-12 the natural way — call `age()` from a per-minute routing tick — and aging remains a no-op. The unit test `aging_decays_by_gamma_per_interval` (prophet.rs:326-349) cannot catch it: it advances the virtual clock by exactly 1 s then 2 s with a 1 s `aging_interval`, and its second assertion `0.99 · 0.5^3` happens to equal the buggy result `(0.99 · 0.5) · 0.5^2`, so the reset is arithmetically invisible.
- **Impact:** Silent, total failure of RFC 6693 Eq. 2 even after DTN-12 is fixed; stale DPs persist indefinitely.
- **Fix:** Advance the baseline only by the whole intervals actually consumed, keeping `t` (the existing `last_meet`) as the base:
```rust
let consumed = cfg.aging_interval.saturating_mul(k.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
aging.push((*dst, aged, if k > 0 { *t + consumed } else { *t }));
```
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** Interacts with DTN-14 (`last_meet` doubles as the Eq. 1 encounter-interval clock). `aging_decays_by_gamma_per_interval` must be rewritten to age at a sub-interval cadence and assert non-decay, then at a super-interval cadence and assert exact `gamma^k`. The Kani proof covers `floor_intervals` alone and stays valid — it does *not* cover the remainder-carry invariant, so a new property test is warranted.

#### DTN-14: `age()` also clobbers the Eq. 1 encounter-interval clock, permanently pinning `P_encounter` at its ceiling
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `9b823e0`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:176-179` (fn `age`) vs `prophet.rs:203-213` (fn `meet`), `prophet.rs:79-87` (fn `p_encounter`)
- **What:** `last_meet` is a single map serving two different semantics: the aging baseline (Eq. 2) and the "time since the previous encounter" used to interval-scale `P_encounter` (Eq. 1). `age()` overwrites it with the aging time, destroying the encounter timestamp.
- **Evidence:**
```
204	        let since = self
205	            .last_meet
206	            .get(other)
207	            .map(|t| now.saturating_sub(*t).as_millis() as u64)
208	            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX); // first encounter → full P_encounter
209	        let p_enc = if self.dps.contains_key(other) {
210	            cfg.p_encounter(since)
82	        if since_ms <= intvl_ms {
83	            self.p_encounter_max
```
- **Why it is wrong:** ROUTE2_DESIGN.md:37 specifies `P_encounter(intvl) = P_encounter_max·(I_typ/intvl)^alpha` for `intvl ≥ I_typ` — the whole point being that *rarely* met peers get a smaller boost. Once `age()` is wired (DTN-12) and runs on a tick, `since` is always ≈ the tick period, which is `<= intvl_ms`, so line 82-83 always returns `p_encounter_max`. Interval scaling is dead, and every peer — met hourly or met once a year — receives the maximum encounter boost.
- **Root cause:** One `HashMap<PeerId, Duration>` reused for two independent clocks.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Aging tick every 60 s, `aging_interval` 1800 s. A peer met once every 12 hours still gets `p_enc = 0.7` instead of `0.7·(1800/43200)^0.5 ≈ 0.143`. DPs for rarely-seen peers inflate ~5×, and `gtmx_advantage` cannot distinguish a good carrier from a bad one.
- **Impact:** Eq. 1 interval scaling is silently disabled; PRoPHET's core discrimination signal is flattened.
- **Fix:** Split into two maps: `last_encounter: HashMap<PeerId, Duration>` (written only by `meet`) and `aging_base: HashMap<PeerId, Duration>` (written only by `age`). Consume them at prophet.rs:204 and prophet.rs:162 respectively.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `age`, `meet`, `prune` (prophet.rs:267-270 retains `last_meet` against `dps` — needs the same treatment for both maps), the `MAX_DP_ENTRIES` eviction at prophet.rs:198-199, and the `first_contact_sets_p_encounter_first` / `direct_update_converges_to_bound` tests.

#### DTN-15: The transitivity loop bypasses `MAX_DP_ENTRIES` entirely — one `meet` from a hostile peer can insert unlimited DP entries
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `e516e42`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:186-239` (fn `meet`)
- **What:** The `MAX_DP_ENTRIES` guard runs **once**, at the top of `meet`, only when `other` is not already known, and it evicts exactly **one** entry. The Eq. 3 transitivity loop that follows then inserts one new entry per element of the caller-supplied `other_predictions` slice, with no cap and no re-check.
- **Evidence:**
```
190	        if self.dps.len() >= MAX_DP_ENTRIES && !self.dps.contains_key(other) {
192	            if let Some((lo_dst, _)) = self
198	                self.dps.remove(&lo_dst);
199	                self.last_meet.remove(&lo_dst);
226	        for (dst, p_other_dst) in other_predictions {
230	            let p_t = p_self_other * p_other_dst.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * cfg.beta;
231	            let p_old_t = self.dps.get(dst).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);
232	            if p_t > p_old_t {
233	                self.dps.insert(*dst, p_t);
234	                self.last_meet.insert(*dst, now);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The module header (prophet.rs:10-11) claims "transitivity fills it toward N, **bounded by `MAX_DP_ENTRIES`**". It is not. `other_predictions` is `&[(PeerId, f64)]`, whose length is entirely peer-controlled — `TOP_N_DP = 32` is only applied to the snapshot this node *sends* (prophet.rs:254, `rows.truncate(TOP_N_DP)`), never to what it *receives*. Nothing between the wire decode and `DeliveryPredictability::meet` re-imposes the limit (`opportunistic.rs:139-141` forwards the slice verbatim; `routing/mod.rs:177` passes `&[]`).
- **Root cause:** Trust that a well-behaved peer sends at most `TOP_N_DP` rows. The cap was never made defensive.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A peer connects once and sends a `CapabilityBundle` carrying 5 000 000 `(PeerId, f64)` rows with random 32-byte `PeerId`s and `p = 1.0`. After a single `meet`, `self.dps` and `self.last_meet` each hold ~5 M entries: 5 M × (32 B key + 8 B value + `HashMap` overhead) × 2 maps ≈ 1 GB. Every entry is above `p_first_threshold` (`p_t = 0.495 · 1.0 · 0.9 = 0.4455`), so `prune()` would not remove any of them, and `age()` (which would eventually decay them) is never called (DTN-12).
- **Impact:** Single-packet remote memory-exhaustion DoS on any node that accepts a contact — the most direct crash primitive found in this scope. It also poisons the snapshot: the 32 rows this node then advertises are attacker-chosen fake peers, propagating the poison network-wide.
- **Fix:** (a) Truncate on ingest: `for (dst, p) in other_predictions.iter().take(TOP_N_DP)`. (b) Move the capacity check *inside* the loop so each insert is bounded:
```rust
if !self.dps.contains_key(dst) && self.dps.len() >= MAX_DP_ENTRIES {
    // only displace an entry strictly worse than p_t, else skip
}
```
  (c) Reject rows whose `p` is not finite rather than relying on `clamp` (`f64::NAN.clamp(0.0,1.0)` returns NaN, and while `NaN > p_old_t` is false today, that is load-bearing behaviour that should be explicit).
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `opportunistic.rs:139-141` (`on_contact`), `sim/mod.rs:424-425`, the DISCO-001 `CapabilityBundle` decoder (which must also cap the row count at the wire level), the test `capped_entries_evict_lowest` (prophet.rs:405-414 — see DTN-16), ROUTING_SECURITY.md.

#### DTN-16: `capped_entries_evict_lowest` is a fake test — a `u8` cast makes it insert 10 entries instead of 4106, so the cap is never exercised
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `e516e42`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:405-414`
- **What:** The loop bound `(MAX_DP_ENTRIES + 10) as u8` truncates: `4106 as u8` = `4106 % 256` = **10**. The loop runs `i in 0..10`, inserting 10 peers, then asserts `p.len() <= 4096` — trivially true.
- **Evidence:**
```
405	    #[test]
406	    fn capped_entries_evict_lowest() {
410	        for i in 0..(MAX_DP_ENTRIES + 10) as u8 {
411	            p.meet(&pid(i), &[]);
412	        }
413	        assert!(p.len() <= MAX_DP_ENTRIES, "cap violated: {}", p.len());
414	    }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The `pid(id: u8)` helper (prophet.rs:291-295) can only produce 256 distinct peers, so this test *cannot* reach 4096 entries by construction. It also never asserts the "evict **lowest**" half of its own name — no DP values are compared before and after. It is the only test covering `MAX_DP_ENTRIES`, and ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md row 1 cites it as the evidence that eviction works (marked "✅ PASS"). The test would still pass if the entire cap block (prophet.rs:190-201) were deleted, and it does not detect DTN-15 at all.
- **Root cause:** `pid` takes `u8`; the author cast the bound to fit rather than widening `pid`.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** N/A (test-quality defect), but it is why DTN-15 shipped.
- **Impact:** False verification evidence: a documented acceptance criterion is backed by a test that exercises 0.24 % of the intended input and asserts a tautology.
- **Fix:** Widen the helper to `fn pid(id: u32)` writing `id.to_le_bytes()` into `b[0..4]`, loop `0..(MAX_DP_ENTRIES as u32 + 10)`, assert `len() == MAX_DP_ENTRIES`, and additionally seed one deliberately low-DP entry and assert it is the one gone. Add a separate test feeding `meet` a 100 000-row `other_predictions` slice and asserting the cap holds (regression for DTN-15).
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md row 1 must be re-run; `REQ-ROUTE-T-010` (ROUTING_REQUIREMENTS.md:178) explicitly requires an eviction test.

#### DTN-17: `gamma.powi(k as i32)` — `u64 → i32` truncation can wrap negative and inflate a DP to `+inf`
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `9b823e0`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:164-168` (fn `age`)
- **What:** `k` is `u64` (from `floor_intervals`, whose input is a `Duration` in nanoseconds) and is cast with `as i32`. Rust integer `as` casts **truncate/wrap**; they do not saturate. A `k` above `2^31` becomes negative, and `gamma < 1` raised to a large negative power is `+inf`.
- **Evidence:**
```
164	            let aged = if k > 0 {
165	                p * cfg.gamma.powi(k as i32)
166	            } else {
167	                *p
168	            };
```
  Verified arithmetic: with `aging_interval = Duration::from_millis(1)` and the SIM virtual clock at unix epoch seconds (`sim/mod.rs:243-244` stores `VIRTUAL_EPOCH_SECS + sim_ms/1000`), `TimePoint::Virtual` (prophet.rs:101-103) returns `1_700_000_000 × 1000 = 1_700_000_000_000` ms. Against a `last_meet` of 0, `k = 1_700_000_000_000`; `1_700_000_000_000 as i32 = -807_049_216`; `0.999f64.powi(-807_049_216) = +inf`.
- **Why it is wrong:** `aged >= cfg.p_first_threshold` (prophet.rs:169) is **true** for `+inf`, so the poisoned value is retained, not discarded. It then propagates through Eq. 3 (`p_t = p_self_other * p_other * beta` at prophet.rs:230 — `inf × finite = inf`) into `snapshot()` and out to every neighbour. `total_cmp` (prophet.rs:251) sorts `inf` first, so the poisoned row always occupies the top of the advertised snapshot. `gtmx_advantage`'s `p_candidate <= p_self + DP_FLOOR_EPS` (opportunistic.rs:155-158) then makes the node believe no carrier can ever beat it.
- **Root cause:** `powi` takes `i32`; the cast was written without a clamp because "k is small in practice".
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Any configuration with a sub-second `aging_interval` (nothing validates the field — `ProphetConfig` is `pub` with public fields and no constructor check), or a `with_virtual_clock` attached *after* a `meet` (prophet.rs:128-132 warns about this in a doc comment only, and `with_virtual_clock` is `pub`), which mixes a wall-clock `elapsed()` baseline near 0 with an absolute-epoch `now`.
- **Impact:** Permanent DP-table poisoning that propagates to the whole neighbourhood; the affected node stops forwarding entirely.
- **Fix:** Clamp before the cast and guard the result:
```rust
let k32 = k.min(i32::MAX as u64) as i32;
let aged = p * cfg.gamma.powi(k32);
let aged = if aged.is_finite() { aged.clamp(0.0, 1.0) } else { 0.0 };
```
  Also validate `ProphetConfig` on construction: `0.0 < gamma < 1.0`, `aging_interval >= 1 s`, `0.0 <= alpha, beta, delta <= 1.0`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `snapshot`, `prune`, `opportunistic.rs::gtmx_advantage`/`decide`, `sim/mod.rs:424`. A Kani proof covering `age`'s exponent clamp would complement `prophet_floor_intervals_division`, which today only proves the division itself and stops short of the `powi` cast.

#### DTN-18: No DP value is ever clamped to `[0, 1]`, and no self-exclusion exists — a peer can make this node believe it is the best carrier for itself
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `e516e42`  ·  2026-08-27
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/prophet.rs:224-237` (Eq. 3 in fn `meet`)
- **What:** Two omissions. (a) The transitivity loop skips only `dst == other`; it has no notion of the **local node's own** `PeerId`, because `DeliveryPredictability` never stores one. A neighbour's snapshot legitimately contains `P(B, A)` where `A` is this node, so `A` inserts a DP row for **itself**. (b) The result `p_t` is written unclamped; only the *input* `p_other_dst` is clamped.
- **Evidence:**
```
226	        for (dst, p_other_dst) in other_predictions {
227	            if dst == other || dst.as_bytes() == other.as_bytes() {
228	                continue;
229	            }
230	            let p_t = p_self_other * p_other_dst.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * cfg.beta;
231	            let p_old_t = self.dps.get(dst).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);
232	            if p_t > p_old_t {
233	                self.dps.insert(*dst, p_t);
```
  Line 227's two conditions are also redundant — `dst == other` and `dst.as_bytes() == other.as_bytes()` are the same test on a `PeerId([u8;32])`.
- **Why it is wrong:** prophet.rs:9 states "`P(A,A) = 1`". Neither `new()` nor `meet()` ever establishes that; instead `P(A,A)` becomes whatever `0.495 · P(B,A) · 0.9` evaluates to, typically ≈ 0.4. This is a real routing hazard: any layer that consults `p_for(dest)` where `dest` happens to be the local node gets a middling value instead of certainty, and the self-row consumes a `MAX_DP_ENTRIES` slot and appears in the outbound `snapshot()` (advertising "I am a 0.4-probability carrier for myself" to the whole mesh). Separately, because `gamma > 1` is not rejected (DTN-17 fix note) and `p_t` is unclamped, DPs can exceed the `1 - delta` bound Eq. 1 is designed to respect.
- **Root cause:** `DeliveryPredictability` is deliberately identity-less ("directional per-destination"), so it cannot filter self.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Normal operation between two honest nodes A and B: B's `snapshot()` includes `(A, 0.495)` because B met A. A's `meet(&B, snap)` reaches line 226 with `dst = A`, which is neither `other` (=B) nor filtered, and inserts `P(A,A) = 0.495 · 0.495 · 0.9 ≈ 0.22`. Every node in the mesh carries a bogus self-row within one contact round.
