#### MG-41: `NotSupported` conflates "hardware absent" with "permission denied" — different user remediations
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `a442d43`  ·  2026-08-27 — added a third variant, `RadioDisabled`, beyond the two the finding's own fix text names. Reclassifying every BLE/Wi-Fi call site surfaced a real third case ("radio present and permitted, but currently switched off" — `BleError::AdapterOff`, both Wi-Fi transports' `!adapter.is_available()`) that fits neither `HardwareUnavailable` nor `PermissionDenied`; the finding's own fix text already names this exact three-way split for the sibling `TransportState` enum (`NoHardware`/`PermissionDenied`/`RadioOff`), so this closes the same gap consistently in `TransportError` rather than forcing a wrong classification. `TransportState::Unavailable` itself remains unsplit (the finding frames that as optional — "or a side-channel reason on the transport"; still out of scope).
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/error.rs:10-12`, `:33`
- **What:** One variant means both "this device has no such radio" and "the user has not granted the permission". The doc comment states both explicitly.
- **Evidence:**
```
 10     /// The transport cannot perform the requested operation in its current
 11     /// state (e.g. BLE adapter not present, permission denied).
 12     NotSupported,
...
 33             TransportError::NotSupported => write!(f, "transport: operation not supported"),
```
The same conflation is baked into `TransportState`:
```
mod.rs:76     /// Hardware off / permission denied / hardware not present.
mod.rs:78     Unavailable = 0,
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The two conditions have opposite remediations and opposite recovery characteristics. "Hardware not present" is permanent for the device — the UI should hide the feature and the manager should never retry (MG-12's backoff ladder would spin forever). "Permission denied" is one user tap away — the UI must show an actionable prompt, and recovery should be immediate on grant. A UI receiving `NotSupported` cannot choose between "Your device does not support LoRa" and "Tap to grant Bluetooth permission", and the `Display` impl at `:33` gives it nothing to work with either.
- **Root cause:** Modelled on the transport's internal view ("I can't do this right now") rather than on the caller's decision ("what do I tell the user, and should I retry?").
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Android 12+ user declines the `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` runtime prompt. `BleTransport` reports `NotSupported`/`Unavailable`. The app surfaces "operation not supported" and the user concludes their phone lacks Bluetooth. A one-tap fix becomes a permanent loss of the mesh's primary bearer.
- **Impact:** Users silently lose the most important transport with a message that actively misleads them. In a disaster-response product, an unnecessary loss of BLE connectivity is a direct safety impact.
- **Fix:**
```rust
/// The required radio/hardware is not present on this device — permanent.
HardwareUnavailable,
/// A required OS permission has not been granted — user-actionable.
PermissionDenied { permission: &'static str },
```
with distinct `Display` strings, and a matching split of `TransportState::Unavailable` into `NoHardware` / `PermissionDenied` / `RadioOff` (or a side-channel reason on the transport) so the UI and the recovery scheduler can both act.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `ble.rs` permission handling, `iris-android/src/bridge.rs` FFI error mapping and the Kotlin permission flow, `TransportState::from_u8`/`as_u8` if the state is also split (an FFI ABI change), all `NotSupported` construction sites.

---

#### MG-42: `TransportError` drops the error source chain and compares by message string
- **Severity:** Low
- **Fix status:** ✅ Fixed  ·  Tier 2  ·  commit `a442d43`  ·  2026-08-27 — resolved via MG-39's `Io{kind,msg}` alone, which the finding's own fix text frames as sufficient ("the derives survive and the kind gives back the machine-readable discriminant"). Did not add a real `source()` chain (`Arc<dyn Error + Send + Sync>` + manual `PartialEq` over discriminant+kind only) — the finding's own fix text marks that as an explicit, separate option ("if a real source() is wanted"), not the core ask, and the added complexity (giving up derived `Eq`/`Hash`) is disproportionate to what MG-39/40 already deliver.
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/error.rs:6`, `:45`, `:47-51`
- **What:** `impl std::error::Error for TransportError {}` is empty, so `source()` returns `None` for every variant including the ones that wrap a real underlying error. And `derive(PartialEq, Eq)` makes equality for `Io`/`Protocol` a comparison of human-readable strings.
- **Evidence:**
```
  6 #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  7 pub enum TransportError {
...
 45 impl std::error::Error for TransportError {}
 46
 47 impl From<std::io::Error> for TransportError {
 48     fn from(e: std::io::Error) -> Self {
 49         TransportError::Io(e.to_string())
 50     }
 51 }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Two consequences. (a) `anyhow`/`eyre`-style chain printing and any `while let Some(e) = e.source()` walk terminate immediately, so the OS-level cause is unavailable in diagnostics — the string at `:49` is the only surviving trace, and once it is embedded in a `Display` it cannot be parsed back. (b) String equality makes tests brittle: `TransportError::Protocol("payload 300 B exceeds LoRa 237-B frame capacity (fragment upstream)")` compares unequal to the same error with a reworded message, so any message edit silently changes program semantics wherever `==` is used on these variants.
- **Root cause:** `Clone + PartialEq + Eq` were derived to make errors easy to assert on in tests; `std::io::Error` supports none of them, forcing the stringification, and `source()` was never implemented because there was no longer a source to return.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A TCP send fails with a nested `os error 104`. `internet.rs` converts it; the operator sees `transport io error: Connection reset by peer (os error 104)` and nothing else — no chain, no kind, no downcast path (see MG-39).
- **Impact:** Degraded production diagnostics and a semantic dependency on log prose. Low severity on its own; it is the structural reason MG-39 and MG-40 cannot be fixed without also revisiting the derives.
- **Fix:** Combined with MG-39's `Io { kind, msg }`, the derives survive and the kind gives back the machine-readable discriminant. If a real `source()` is wanted, box the cause behind an `Arc<dyn Error + Send + Sync>` and implement `PartialEq` manually over the discriminant + kind only, never over the message.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** Every `assert_eq!` on a `TransportError` (`manager.rs:519-522`, `:580-583`, and the transport test modules); `iris-android` FFI error mapping.

---

### Cross-cutting notes

**Answer to Priority Target #1 (failover).** When a transport dies mid-send, an in-flight message is **neither silently dropped nor hung** — `message_engine::deliver_outbound` (`:1251-1276`) treats a failed `send()` as `sent_any == false` and re-queues via `requeue_or_fail`. But there is no *failover*: for P2–P7 the manager returns exactly one transport (MG-5), so the message waits a full retry backoff and the deterministic selector then re-picks the same dead transport, because nothing marks it (no per-transport circuit breaker) and nothing distinguishes a permanent refusal from a transient one (MG-40). Two adjacent hazards found on the same path: (a) `Transport::send()` has **no timeout anywhere** in the production path — `grep` shows `tokio::time::timeout` only in tests and in `internet.rs`'s connect/read paths (`:267`, `:291`, `:302`), never around a send — and `spawn_delivery_loop` (`message_engine/mod.rs:1142-1154`) awaits `deliver_outbound` sequentially, so one transport blocking in `send()` stalls the **entire outbound queue including P0 SOS** for as long as it blocks (a TCP `write_all` to a dead peer can block for minutes); (b) partial-fragment success (`:1238-1254`) sets `sent_any = true` if *any* fragment succeeds, so a message that lost fragment 3 of 10 is marked `InTransit` and never re-queued, and the receiver can never reassemble it. Both sit just outside the four scope files but are reachable only through the manager's API shape and should be fixed alongside MG-5 and MG-13.

**Answer to Priority Target #2 (gateway trust).** No field of a gateway advertisement is authenticated (MG-25). The upstream gate checks that a signature is *present*, never that it is *valid*, and the function containing that gate has no production caller at all. The single input that grants gateway status is a plaintext string tag. There is no liveness probe before election, no reputation gate at admission, and the blacklist that does exist is erased whenever the subject leaves the neighbour table (MG-26). The registry *is* bounded at 64 entries, so the "unbounded RAM" hypothesis does not hold — but the eviction policy favours the attacker (MG-35). The practical severity is currently capped only by the fact that the whole engine is unwired (MG-30); fix MG-25 through MG-29 **before** wiring it.


## 12. Area F — Network simulator, ML experiment harness and observability

# R1 — Simulation & Observability deep bug hunt (iris-core)

#### SIM-1: Simulator forwarding order is non-deterministic because SCF buffer keys tie-break on wall-clock UUIDv7
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:691` (fn `build_envelope`) + `crates/iris-core/src/routing/scf.rs:57-71,87,370-372`
- **What:** The whole SIM-001 acceptance ("same seed → same result anchor") rests on a deterministic forward order. `ordered_buffered()` returns `self.buffer.values()` from a `BTreeMap<StoreKey, _>`; `StoreKey = (priority_rank, expiry_unix, message_id)`. In every sim scenario the injected messages share a priority and (because the clock is quantised to whole seconds, SIM-4) an identical `expiry_unix`, so ordering is decided entirely by `message_id`, which `build_envelope` mints with `MessageId::new_v7()` — a UUIDv7 built from the **host wall clock plus 74 random bits**. The seed does not control it.
- **Evidence:**
```
sim/mod.rs:691            message_id: MessageId::new_v7(),
scf.rs:57  pub struct StoreKey {
scf.rs:58      pub priority_rank: u8, // 0 = P0, 7 = P7
scf.rs:59      pub expiry_unix: u64,  // sooner expiry = smaller
scf.rs:60      pub message_id: MessageId,
scf.rs:87      buffer: BTreeMap<StoreKey, StoredMessage>,
scf.rs:370  pub fn ordered_buffered(&self) -> Vec<StoredMessage> {
scf.rs:371      self.buffer.values().cloned().collect()
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `sim/mod.rs:4-5` states "over a *virtual clock* so every run is reproducible (same seed → same result anchor, acceptance criterion)". A wall-clock+random tiebreak makes the message visit order in `run()` (mod.rs:602-607) vary between runs, changing (a) the order RNG loss draws are consumed (`is_lost`, mod.rs:248-254), (b) which node wins a spray budget (mod.rs:509-517), (c) which copy reaches the recipient first.
- **Root cause:** The sim reuses the production `ScfEngine`/`Envelope` types and inherited their production id generator instead of minting seeded ids from its own `ChaCha8Rng`.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `sim_scenarios.rs:105 loss_reduces_delivery_ratio_monotonically` runs with 60% loss; the set of dropped messages depends on visit order and therefore on wall time. Run the suite twice a millisecond apart and the delivered set can differ.
- **Impact:** Every determinism assertion in the suite is vacuous (see SIM-2). A routing regression that manifests only under one forward ordering is intermittently green, and a "reproducible result anchor" recorded in SIM_VERIFICATION.md cannot actually be reproduced.
- **Fix:** Mint sim message ids from the seeded RNG: in `build_envelope` replace `MessageId::new_v7()` with `MessageId::from_bytes(rng.gen())` (needs `&mut self`), or derive from `(seed, injection_index)`. Alternatively give `StoreKey` a deterministic monotone `seq: u64` ahead of `message_id`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** All of `tests/sim_scenarios.rs`, `tests/ml_experiments.rs` (AC-1/AC-2/AC-5 hinge on this), `sim/mod.rs::same_seed_same_result_anchor`, `routing/scf.rs` key ordering.

#### SIM-2: `result_anchor` is too weak to detect any behavioural change, so all "determinism" tests are near-tautologies
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:674`; asserted at `tests/sim_scenarios.rs:96-102,196-199` and `tests/ml_experiments.rs:80,90,188-218`
- **What:** The anchor is `format!("sim-{}-d{}-i{}", seed, delivered_total, injected_total)` — seed plus two counts. Two runs that deliver the same *number* of messages by completely different routes, hop counts, latencies and relay counts produce an identical anchor.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:674  result_anchor: format!("sim-{}-d{}-i{}", self.seed, delivered_total, injected_total),
ml_experiments.rs:90   assert_eq!(shadowed.result_anchor, base.result_anchor);
sim_scenarios.rs:96    assert_eq!(run_dense(99).result_anchor, run_dense(99).result_anchor);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The module header (mod.rs:4-5) sells the anchor as the reproducibility acceptance criterion. `injected_total` is a pure function of the scenario definition, so half the anchor is constant by construction; the only varying field is a delivery count that saturates at 100% in most scenarios.
- **Root cause:** Anchor was defined as a human-readable label rather than a run fingerprint.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Under SIM-1, dense_mesh always delivers everything, so the anchor is stable even though internal ordering is not — the determinism test cannot fail.
- **Impact:** `determinism_same_seed_same_anchor`, `route2_opportunistic_deterministic_same_seed`, and `ac5_ten_seeds_reproducible_both_regimes` all still pass with a deliberately randomised router.
- **Fix:** Hash the full ordered event trace into the anchor: for each delivery push `(message_id, delivering_node_index, at_ms, hops)` into a sorted list and digest it, plus `relays_total` and the latency vector.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/metrics.rs:92` copies the anchor; the two test files above; SIM_VERIFICATION.md anchors need regenerating.

#### SIM-3: `ac5_ten_seeds_reproducible_both_regimes` asserts 20 distinct anchors — the seed is literally in the string
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/tests/ml_experiments.rs:223-232`
- **What:** The test claims to prove "no seed collision" by deduping anchor strings. Since `result_anchor` begins `sim-{seed}-` (mod.rs:674) and the two regimes have different injected counts, the 20 strings are distinct no matter what the simulator does.
- **Evidence:**
```
ml_experiments.rs:223    // Distinct seeds must produce distinct anchors (no seed collision).
ml_experiments.rs:228    assert_eq!(
ml_experiments.rs:229        uniq.len(), 20,
ml_experiments.rs:231        "10 seeds x 2 regimes must give 20 distinct anchors"
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The intended invariant is "different seeds explore different trajectories". Comparing strings that embed the seed tests nothing.
- **Root cause:** Anchor doubles as identifier and fingerprint.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Hard-code `rng = ChaCha8Rng::seed_from_u64(0)` in `Simulation::new` and this test still passes.
- **Impact:** ML-001 AC-5 is unverified.
- **Fix:** Compare the SIM-2 trace hash with the seed prefix stripped; assert at least K of 10 seeds differ.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** Depends on SIM-2's fix.

#### SIM-4: The virtual clock is quantised to whole seconds, so TTL, message age and expiry are blind to sub-second sim time
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:242-246` (fn `advance_to`)
- **What:** `advance_to` stores `VIRTUAL_EPOCH_SECS + sim_ms / 1000` into the shared `AtomicU64` clock. Every consumer (`ScfEngine::now_unix`, TTL expiry in `buffer_message`, `shadow_features` age/ttl_frac at mod.rs:285-288, PRoPHET DP aging) sees an integer-second clock while the event timeline runs in milliseconds.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:242  fn advance_to(&mut self, sim_ms: u64) {
mod.rs:243      self.now_ms = sim_ms;
mod.rs:244      self.clock
mod.rs:245          .store(VIRTUAL_EPOCH_SECS + sim_ms / 1000, Ordering::Relaxed);
mod.rs:246  }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Truncating division makes all events in `[n*1000, n*1000+999]` share one timestamp. Combined with `StoreKey.expiry_unix` (scf.rs:67) it collapses the ordering key (SIM-1), and `age_s` (mod.rs:286) is 0 for every message younger than a second, so feature slots 5 and 6 are degenerate.
- **Root cause:** The production `ScfEngine` clock contract is seconds; the sim adapted by truncating instead of carrying millisecond resolution.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `vehicle_relay`'s `+300` ms backbone links (scenario.rs:92-97) and `periodic_ferry`'s `step_ms/2` offsets (scenario.rs:196-200) produce zero clock movement.
- **Impact:** TTL expiry can never fire mid-second; LP features 5/6 carry almost no signal on ferry scenarios, weakening AC-3.
- **Fix:** Give `ScfEngine`/`OpportunisticRouter` a millisecond virtual clock, or at minimum store `sim_ms` and divide only at the TTL comparison.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/scf.rs` `with_virtual_clock`, `routing/opportunistic.rs` `with_virtual_clock`, `sim/ml/features.rs`.

#### SIM-5: `SimNode.evictions` is read in two places and written in none — the eviction metric is always zero
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:47` (field), read at `mod.rs:619` and `sim/metrics.rs:72`
- **What:** `SimNode::new` sets `evictions: 0` (mod.rs:66) and nothing ever increments it. `SimOutcome.evictions_total` and `SimMetrics.evictions_total` are constant 0. The simulator also never calls `ScfEngine::evict_to_fit` or `reap_expired`, so no storage pressure or TTL reaping is ever applied.
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "\.evictions" crates/ --include=*.rs` →
```
crates/iris-core/src/sim/metrics.rs:72:            evictions_total += n.evictions;
crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:619:            evictions_total += node.evictions;
```
(no write site anywhere; `grep -rn "evict_to_fit\|reap_expired" crates/iris-core/src/sim/` returns nothing)
- **Why it is wrong:** `sim/metrics.rs:3-5` names "storage utilization, and eviction counts" as "the acceptance metrics for the ≥3 reproducible sim scenarios", and mod.rs:11-12 promises the same. Both are fabricated.
- **Root cause:** The eviction path was scaffolded on the outcome struct and never wired to the SCF engine.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Set `storage_max_bytes` to 1 on every node and run `pilot_nct_of_n(100, 10, 7)` — delivery stays 100% and `evictions_total` stays 0.
- **Impact:** SIM-001 cannot detect a buffer-management regression; SCF eviction policy (priority ranking, P0 exemption) is entirely unexercised by the sim harness.
- **Fix:** In `run()`'s contact branch, after each `buffer_message`, call `evict_to_fit(node.storage_max_bytes)` and add `node.evictions += evicted.len() as u64`; call `reap_expired()` at each timeline tick.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/scf.rs:302,329`; every scenario's delivery ratio changes once eviction is armed — SIM_VERIFICATION.md numbers need regenerating.

#### SIM-6: `peak_storage_bytes` is not a peak — it is the final usage after the run
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/metrics.rs:38-39,67-73` (fn `from_outcome`)
- **What:** Documented "Max buffered bytes observed across nodes" but computed once from `SimOutcome.nodes` after `run()` returned, so it is `max over nodes of usage at t=end`, never a maximum over time.
- **Evidence:**
```
metrics.rs:38    /// Max buffered bytes observed across nodes (proxy for storage util).
metrics.rs:39    pub peak_storage_bytes: u64,
metrics.rs:69    for n in &out.nodes {
metrics.rs:70        let used = n.scf.usage_bytes();
metrics.rs:71        peak_storage_bytes = peak_storage_bytes.max(used);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Device storage sizing depends on the transient high-water mark during a partition, not the residue after healing.
- **Root cause:** Sampling placed at the aggregation site instead of inside the timeline loop.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `pilot_partition_heal(4, 60_000, 99)` buffers all cross-partition traffic until t=60 s then delivers; final usage is near-empty.
- **Impact:** Capacity/scale conclusions under-report; a storage-exhaustion regression is invisible.
- **Fix:** Track a running `peak_storage_bytes` on `Simulation`, updated after each contact tick, and carry it on `SimOutcome`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `SimOutcome` struct, `sim/metrics.rs`.

#### SIM-7: The simulator implements its own forwarding pipeline and never calls the production `RoutingEngine`
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:297-403` (fn `forward_to`), `mod.rs:438-519` (fn `opportunistic_forward`) vs `crates/iris-core/src/routing/mod.rs:63-75` (`ForwardingDecision`), `routing/mod.rs:277-295` (`decide_opportunistic`)
- **What:** `grep -rn "RoutingEngine\|NeighborTable\|ForwardingDecision\|decide_opportunistic" crates/iris-core/src/sim/` returns **nothing**. The sim hand-rolls its own decision cascade (terminal check, no-backtrack, dedup, buffer dedup, hop budget, DP/spray) inside `forward_to`. It borrows only leaf primitives (`max_hops_for_priority`, `ForwardedCache`, `ScfEngine`, `OpportunisticRouter::decide`). The production `RoutingEngine::decide` — Algorithm 1 Direct, Algorithm 2 KnownPath, Algorithm 3 Flood, Algorithm 4 Store, plus neighbour-table lookup, route pruning and telemetry — is never exercised.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:307        if msg.delivery_status.is_terminal() { return ForwardResult::Sinked; }
mod.rs:311        if msg.received_from == Some(dst_peer) { return ForwardResult::Blocked; }
mod.rs:315        if self.nodes[dst].forwarded.is_duplicate(&id) { return ForwardResult::Sinked; }
mod.rs:319        if self.nodes[dst].scf.delivery_status(&id).is_some() { return ForwardResult::Sinked; }
mod.rs:323        let budget = max_hops_for_priority(msg.envelope.priority).max_hops;
mod.rs:325        if hops >= budget { return ForwardResult::Blocked; }
routing/mod.rs:63 pub enum ForwardingDecision { Forward{..}, Flood{..}, Store, Drop }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `sim/mod.rs:3-4` claims the sim "Drives the real ROUTE-001 (hop budgets, `ForwardedCache` anti-loop) and SCF-001 (`ScfEngine`) logic". It drives two of ROUTE-001's primitives, not ROUTE-001. Anything living in `RoutingEngine` — Direct/KnownPath/Flood selection, the neighbour-table freshness window, `ROUTING_DECISIONS_TOTAL` telemetry, `prune()` — has zero simulation coverage.
- **Root cause:** `RoutingEngine::decide` is `async` and takes a `&NeighborTable`; the sim is a synchronous discrete-event loop, so the author reimplemented the parts needed rather than adapting.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Invert the hop-budget comparison in `RoutingEngine`, or break Algorithm 3's recipient list, and every sim scenario stays green.
- **Impact:** This is the headline gap. The brief says to use the simulator to review routing/transport logic first; in fact the simulator validates a *parallel reimplementation*. All nine `sim_scenarios.rs` tests, all four PILOT B-1..B-4 tests (`scenario.rs:441-631`) and the ROUTE-002 acceptance tests give confidence about `sim/mod.rs`, not about `routing/mod.rs`. Two forwarding policies now exist and can drift silently.
- **Fix:** Make `RoutingEngine::decide` the single decision authority. Extract the cascade into a synchronous `fn decide_sync(&mut self, ctx: &RouteCtx) -> ForwardingDecision` in `routing/mod.rs`; have both the async wrapper and `Simulation::forward_to` call it, feeding the sim a `NeighborTable` populated from the active contact set.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/mod.rs`, `routing/flood.rs`, `discovery/neighbor_table.rs`, every sim scenario baseline.

#### SIM-8: The discrete-event simulator models no transport at all — no latency, bandwidth, MTU, reordering, duplication, corruption, or mid-transfer disconnect
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:114-118` (`SimLoss`), `mod.rs:582-608` (contact branch of `run`)
- **What:** A contact is an instantaneous, infinite-bandwidth, perfectly-ordered exchange of *every* buffered message in both directions. The entire modelled failure surface is one global `SimLoss { rate: f32 }`. Missing, exhaustively: per-link/per-direction loss (so no **asymmetric links** — A hears B iff B hears A), latency fixed or jittered (delivery timestamp is the contact timestamp, mod.rs:393), bandwidth/throughput ceilings, MTU / max-message-size enforcement, message **reordering**, **duplicate delivery**, corruption, partial or fragmented delivery, mid-transfer disconnect, connect failure, transport-Unavailable transitions, peer churn, LoRa duty-cycle limits, and satellite contact windows.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:115  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
mod.rs:116  pub struct SimLoss {
mod.rs:117      pub rate: f32,
mod.rs:118  }
mod.rs:600            let a_msgs: Vec<_> = self.nodes[a].scf.ordered_buffered();
mod.rs:601            let b_msgs: Vec<_> = self.nodes[b].scf.ordered_buffered();
mod.rs:602            for m in &a_msgs { self.forward_to(a, b, m); }
mod.rs:603            for m in &b_msgs { self.forward_to(b, a, m); }
mod.rs:393                self.nodes[dst].delivered.push((id, self.now_ms));
```
- **Why it is wrong:** A separate `transport::simulated::SimConfig` (`transport/simulated.rs:28-36`) already carries `bandwidth_bps`, `latency_base_ms`, `latency_spread_ms`, and the transport advertises `max_message_size: 64 * 1024` (simulated.rs:77) — but the discrete-event `Simulation` is a disjoint code path that uses none of it. The two "simulators" do not compose.
- **Root cause:** SIM-001 was scoped as a store-carry-forward/contact-schedule model; the transport plane was left to the per-connection `SimulatedTransport`.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A message larger than the radio MTU, or a 50-message backlog drained across a 3-second BLE contact at 20 kbps, is delivered fully and instantly in the sim; on hardware most of it never transfers.
- **Impact:** Falsely reassured tests: `pilot_b1_nct_of_n_scales_to_100` (scenario.rs:464) asserts 100/100 delivery at N=100 across a full mesh — in reality ~4950 simultaneous pairwise contacts each draining a full buffer at zero airtime cost. `pilot_b3_mule_chain_delivers_within_contact_window` (scenario.rs:556) asserts exact-millisecond latency `segments*1000`, true only with zero transfer time. `route2_spray_bounds_overhead_property` measures overhead in message counts, not bytes or airtime. Every latency percentile in `SimMetrics` is a contact-schedule artefact, not a latency measurement.
- **Fix:** Minimum viable fidelity, in order: (1) per-contact byte budget = `bandwidth_bps * contact_duration`, stop forwarding when exhausted; (2) per-direction loss (`SimLoss` keyed by ordered pair `(a,b)`) for asymmetry; (3) reject messages over a configurable `mtu_bytes`; (4) add `latency_base_ms + jitter` to the delivery timestamp instead of using `now_ms`; (5) a `duplicate_rate` and a seeded reorder shuffle of `ordered_buffered`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/metrics.rs` latency percentiles, all scenario expectations in `scenario.rs:394-631`, `tests/sim_scenarios.rs`, `transport/simulated.rs` (merge candidate).

#### SIM-9: `ContactEvent` is an instant, not a window — contact duration is unmodelled, so "contact window" assertions are fiction
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:75-81` (`ContactEvent`), asserted at `crates/iris-core/src/sim/scenario.rs:556-582`
- **What:** `ContactEvent { at_ms, a, b }` has no duration field. Scenario builders emulate a "window" by scheduling two events 500 ms apart (`dense_mesh`, scenario.rs:20-25). Nothing bounds how much can be transferred and nothing models a contact *ending* mid-transfer.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:76  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
mod.rs:77  pub struct ContactEvent {
mod.rs:78      pub at_ms: u64,
mod.rs:79      pub a: usize,
mod.rs:80      pub b: usize,
mod.rs:81  }
scenario.rs:347  /// delivered at `segments*1000` ms — the contact-window expectation
scenario.rs:579        assert_eq!(delivered_at, segments as u64 * 1000);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The B-3 comment says "latency == legs × per-leg window (1000 ms each)", but 1000 ms is the *spacing between instantaneous events*, not a window. The dominant real-world failure — the peer walks out of range halfway through the transfer — cannot be represented.
- **Root cause:** Discrete instants were simpler than intervals for the first cut of the timeline.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A 5-second BLE contact carrying 40 kB. The sim carries an unbounded backlog; hardware carries what fits.
- **Impact:** `pilot_b3_mule_chain_delivers_within_contact_window` and `pilot_b4_ios_limited_relay_participates_on_windows` (scenario.rs:585) assert exact delivery-millisecond values that are pure schedule arithmetic. AC-9/AC-10 are not actually validated.
- **Fix:** Add `duration_ms: u64` to `ContactEvent`; emit paired start/end markers on the timeline; enforce the SIM-8 byte budget across the window and drop the in-flight message when the window closes.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** All of `scenario.rs`, `tests/sim_scenarios.rs`, PILOT_001_DESIGN.md AC-7..AC-10 evidence.

#### SIM-10: `ForwardedCache` ages on `Instant::now()` (real time), so the sim's anti-loop cache never expires — `loop_free()` is guaranteed by construction
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:44,315,377` + `crates/iris-core/src/routing/dedup_cache.rs:19,54-60,63-71`
- **What:** Every `SimNode` carries a `ForwardedCache::default()` whose exact-set retention window is `EXACT_WINDOW = 3600 s`, measured with `Instant::now()` — **real** monotonic time, not the sim's virtual clock. A sim run finishes in microseconds of real time, so the window never elapses and the anti-loop set is permanent for the whole run, however long the virtual timeline.
- **Evidence:**
```
dedup_cache.rs:19  const EXACT_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3600); // 1 h
dedup_cache.rs:57      self.ring.push_back((id, Instant::now()));
dedup_cache.rs:64      let cutoff = Instant::now() - EXACT_WINDOW;
sim/mod.rs:44      pub forwarded: ForwardedCache,
sim/mod.rs:315     if self.nodes[dst].forwarded.is_duplicate(&id) { return ForwardResult::Sinked; }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** SIM-001's headline evidence is "no-loop evidence" (`mod.rs:12`, `SimOutcome::loop_free`, asserted in nine tests). In production a message with TTL 7200 s (`inject_sos`, scenario.rs:256) outlives the 3600 s dedup window, after which a re-encountered copy is no longer a duplicate and can loop. The simulator structurally cannot reach that state.
- **Root cause:** `ScfEngine` and `OpportunisticRouter` were given `with_virtual_clock`; `ForwardedCache` was not, so it silently kept wall time.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Inject a P0 SOS with TTL 7200 s into a ferry scenario with a 20 000 s virtual timeline; the sim reports loop-free, production would re-forward once the real dedup window lapses.
- **Impact:** `loop_free()` proves only "no two terminal deliveries of the same id within one process", which is nearly unfalsifiable. The ROUTE-001 anti-loop guarantee under long TTLs is unverified. It is also a second real-time dependency inside a "virtual clock" simulator (cf. SIM-1).
- **Fix:** Add `ForwardedCache::with_virtual_clock(Arc<AtomicU64>)` mirroring `ScfEngine`, store virtual seconds in the ring instead of `Instant`, wire it in `SimNode::new`, then add a scenario whose virtual span exceeds `EXACT_WINDOW`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/dedup_cache.rs`, `sim/mod.rs:58-72`, every `loop_free()` assertion.

#### SIM-11: `ForwardResult` is computed on every forward and discarded — the enum is dead and the sim cannot count blocked/sinked forwards
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:120-127` (enum `ForwardResult`), produced by `forward_to` (mod.rs:297-403), discarded at `mod.rs:602-607`
- **What:** `forward_to` carefully distinguishes `Delivered` / `Relayed` / `Blocked` / `Sinked`, and the caller throws all of it away.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:602            for m in &a_msgs {
mod.rs:603                self.forward_to(a, b, m);
mod.rs:604            }
mod.rs:605            for m in &b_msgs {
mod.rs:606                self.forward_to(b, a, m);
mod.rs:607            }
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The distinction between "blocked by hop budget", "blocked by loss", "blocked by GTMX+ withholding" and "already held" is exactly the signal needed to explain a low delivery ratio — so much so that `tests/sim_scenarios.rs:125-172` adds a whole `#[ignore]`d `route2_debug_undelivered` helper with `eprintln!` to recover it by brute force.
- **Root cause:** The enum was added for readability inside `forward_to` and never surfaced.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A ROUTE-002 change that makes GTMX+ withhold everything drops delivery, and no metric says why.
- **Impact:** No observability into forwarding outcomes; debugging happens through ignored eprintln tests. `Blocked` also conflates loss with policy, so a loss-model regression looks like a routing regression.
- **Fix:** Tally results into four `u64` counters on `Simulation`, expose on `SimOutcome`, and split `Blocked` into `BlockedHopBudget` / `BlockedLoss` / `BlockedNoAdvantage` / `BlockedBacktrack`. Then delete `route2_debug_undelivered`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `SimOutcome`, `sim/metrics.rs`, `tests/sim_scenarios.rs:125-172`.

#### SIM-12: Contacts sort before injections at the same timestamp, so a message injected at time T misses the contact at time T
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:530-542,555-557` (fn `run`)
- **What:** The timeline is `Vec<(u64, u8)>` with `0 = contact`, `1 = injection`, sorted by `(t, kind)`. At equal `at_ms` the contact marker sorts first, so the contact is fully processed before the message exists in any buffer.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:523        // Event timeline: (sim_ms, kind) — 0 = contact, 1 = injection.
mod.rs:534                timeline.push((c.at_ms, 0));
mod.rs:540            timeline.push((i.at_ms, 1));
mod.rs:542        timeline.sort_unstable_by_key(|(t, k)| (*t, *k));
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Nothing documents this choice, and the opposite convention (inject, then let the contact carry it) is what a scenario author will assume. `community_ferry` schedules intra-community contacts at `t=100` (scenario.rs:123) while `tests/sim_scenarios.rs:117` calls `inject_standard(&mut sim, 2, 100, 7200)` — start_ms is exactly 100, so the first contact round is wasted for the k=0 messages.
- **Root cause:** The kind tag was chosen for the dedup logic (contacts deduped per timestamp, injections not) and doubles as a sort key by accident.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Any scenario where injection time coincides with a contact time; the message waits a full period.
- **Impact:** Latency percentiles in the ferry scenarios are inflated by one period; an L0-vs-L2 overhead comparison picks up an artefact. Silent and easy to trip over when writing a new scenario.
- **Fix:** Flip the tags (`0 = injection`, `1 = contact`), or sort by an explicitly named `kind_priority` constant with a doc comment stating the convention.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `scenario.rs` builders sharing timestamps with `inject_standard`, ferry latency baselines in `tests/sim_scenarios.rs` and `tests/ml_experiments.rs`.

#### SIM-13: Label leakage — the LP training labels come from the whole run, including test-window deliveries, in direct violation of the documented leakage guard
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/ml/experiment.rs:57-75` (fn `run_shadow_experiment`), fed by `crates/iris-core/tests/ml_experiments.rs:24-29,112-113`
- **What:** The split of *samples* is temporal, but the *labels* are not. `delivered_ids` is built from `SimOutcome.nodes[..].delivered` — the complete delivery log of the whole timeline — and is then used to label the train slice. A train-window shadow decision about message M is labelled `true` whenever M was eventually delivered, even if that delivery happened deep inside the test window.
- **Evidence:**
```
ml_experiments.rs:24  fn delivered_ids(out: &SimOutcome) -> HashSet<MessageId> {
ml_experiments.rs:25      out.nodes.iter()
ml_experiments.rs:26          .flat_map(|n| n.delivered.iter().map(|(id, _)| *id))
ml_experiments.rs:27          .collect()
experiment.rs:62      let train: Vec<&ShadowDecision> = samples.iter().filter(|s| s.at_ms <  split_at_ms).collect();
experiment.rs:63      let test:  Vec<&ShadowDecision> = samples.iter().filter(|s| s.at_ms >= split_at_ms).collect();
experiment.rs:72      let labelled = |s: &ShadowDecision| delivered_ids.contains(&s.msg_id);
experiment.rs:73      let fit_data: Vec<(FeatureVec, bool)> = train.iter().map(|s| (s.features, labelled(s))).collect();
experiment.rs:75      let predictor = LinearPredictor::fit(&fit_data);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** `docs/implementation/ML_DESIGN.md:143-149` states the leakage guard verbatim: "the *fit* must never see test-window deliveries. Both slices are emitted from one `Simulation::run` pass; the predictor is frozen before test-time shadow decisions begin." The predictor is indeed frozen (`fit` is called once, before `agreement` on test — that part is correct), but its supervision signal is drawn from the future. `LinearPredictor::fit`'s own doc comment (`predictor.rs:42-44`) repeats the same claim.
- **Root cause:** `delivered_ids` has no timestamp, only ids — `SimNode.delivered` is `Vec<(MessageId, u64)>` and the `u64` delivery time is discarded by the helper. The API makes the correct thing impossible to express.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** `ac3_lp_agrees_with_l2_on_ferry_test_window` with `split_at_ms = 7000` — `community_ferry(4,4,1,2500,·)` schedules contacts out to t=14 000, so a large share of deliveries land after the split and still label train samples.
- **Impact:** Both reported LP numbers are optimistically biased. AC-3's `decision_agreement >= 0.70` and the Brier score are not honest generalization estimates, so the shadow arm cannot be trusted as evidence that L3 would be safe to promote out of shadow mode. This is the one metric the whole ML-001 work package exists to produce.
- **Fix:** Pass delivery *times*, not ids: `delivered_at: &HashMap<MessageId, u64>`, and label a train sample `true` only when `delivered_at.get(&s.msg_id).is_some_and(|t| *t < split_at_ms)`. Add a regression test asserting a message delivered only after the split is labelled `false` in train.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/ml/experiment.rs`, `tests/ml_experiments.rs:112-113`, `ML_VERIFICATION.md` AC-3 numbers must be regenerated; `sim/ml/mod.rs` `ShadowDecision` may need the delivery time plumbed through.

#### SIM-14: Group leakage — the same `msg_id` appears in both train and test slices, so the model memorises per-message outcomes
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/ml/experiment.rs:62-63,72`
- **What:** A single message generates one `ShadowDecision` per (src,dst) relay-candidate evaluation across the whole run (`sim/mod.rs:354-363`). Splitting purely on `at_ms` puts early decisions about message M in train and later decisions about the *same* M in test — with an identical label, since the label is a per-message constant.
- **Evidence:**
```
experiment.rs:62      let train = samples.iter().filter(|s| s.at_ms <  split_at_ms)...
experiment.rs:63      let test  = samples.iter().filter(|s| s.at_ms >= split_at_ms)...
experiment.rs:72      let labelled = |s: &ShadowDecision| delivered_ids.contains(&s.msg_id);
sim/mod.rs:355                rec.record(ShadowDecision { msg_id: id, at_ms: self.now_ms, src, dst, ... });
```
- **Why it is wrong:** ML_DESIGN.md:141-146 dismisses a grouped hold-out ("No per-destination held-out trick is needed"), reasoning about the *contact schedule* distribution — but the label is keyed on message identity, not on the schedule, so message-level grouping is exactly what is needed here.
- **Root cause:** The split criterion was chosen for the contact schedule and applied unchanged to per-message labels.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** In `community_ferry`, TTL is 7200 s and messages injected at t=100 are still being relayed at t=14 000 — every long-lived message straddles the split.
- **Impact:** Compounds SIM-13; test-slice agreement/Brier are further inflated. Fixing SIM-13 alone does not remove this.
- **Fix:** Group-aware split: assign each `msg_id` wholly to train or test (e.g. by first-decision time), or report a second metric restricted to messages that appear only on one side of the split.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/ml/experiment.rs`, `tests/ml_experiments.rs` AC-3 threshold.

#### SIM-15: `agreement()` takes a `_labelled` closure it never uses — "decision agreement" measures agreement with L2, and the threshold sweep optimises for that, not for delivery
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/ml/experiment.rs:110-124` (fn `agreement`), called at `experiment.rs:82,90`
- **What:** The function signature accepts a label closure and discards it (`_labelled`). It compares the thresholded L3 score against `s.l2_decided`. The train-slice threshold sweep (experiment.rs:78-88) therefore picks the threshold that best *imitates PRoPHET GTMX+*, even though the model's weights were fitted against delivery labels.
- **Evidence:**
```
experiment.rs:110  fn agreement(
experiment.rs:111      samples: &[&ShadowDecision],
experiment.rs:113      threshold: f32,
experiment.rs:114      _labelled: impl Fn(&ShadowDecision) -> bool,
experiment.rs:121          .filter(|s| (predictor.score(&s.features) >= threshold) == s.l2_decided)
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Objective mismatch: weights minimise delivery-prediction error, the threshold maximises L2 mimicry. A high `decision_agreement` then reads as "L3 reproduces L2", which is not evidence that L3 is *better* — yet AC-3 treats `>= 0.70` as the pass gate. The dead parameter is also a live compile-silenced hint that the two objectives were conflated during authoring.
- **Root cause:** The function was probably first written to compute label accuracy and later repurposed, leaving the parameter behind.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A predictor that ignores its features entirely and returns a constant just above/below the threshold can score high agreement whenever L2's decisions are lopsided.
- **Impact:** AC-3 does not measure what its name implies; there is no accuracy/precision/recall/F1 anywhere in the codebase (`grep -rn "precision\|recall\|f1_score" crates/iris-core/src/sim/` → nothing) even though ML_DESIGN.md §7 lists "Predicted-delivery accuracy" as an L3-specific metric.
- **Fix:** Drop the unused parameter; add a separate `label_accuracy` (and precision/recall/F1 with explicit empty-class guards) computed against `labelled`, and calibrate the threshold on *that*, reporting L2 agreement as a distinct diagnostic.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/ml/experiment.rs`, `MlMetrics` struct, `tests/ml_experiments.rs:118-121`, ML_VERIFICATION.md §7.

#### SIM-16: `evaluate_gt` never dedups contact times, so a duplicate timestamp injects a zero interval that drags the learned period down
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/ml/experiment.rs:152-174` (fn `evaluate_gt`) and `crates/iris-core/src/sim/ml/predictor.rs:80-101` (`GtPredictor::fit`)
- **What:** Both sort defensively but neither dedups. A gateway node in more than one contact at the same `at_ms` yields `w[1]-w[0] == 0`, a zero interval that enters both the median (GT) and the mean (static baseline).
- **Evidence:**
```
experiment.rs:155      let mut sorted: Vec<u64> = gateway_contact_times_ms.to_vec();
experiment.rs:156      sorted.sort_unstable();
experiment.rs:173      let intervals: Vec<f64> = train.windows(2).map(|w| (w[1] - w[0]) as f64).collect();
predictor.rs:84        times.sort_unstable();
predictor.rs:85        let mut intervals: Vec<f64> = times.windows(2).map(|w| (w[1] - w[0]) as f64).collect();
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The unit test at `experiment.rs:207-208` explicitly says "The outlier must not collide with an existing timestamp or `dedup` collapses it" — the author believed a dedup exists in this path. It does not; only the *test helper* `gateway_contact_times` in `tests/ml_experiments.rs:130-139` calls `.dedup()`. So the library is only correct because every current caller happens to dedup for it.
- **Root cause:** Dedup responsibility was placed in the caller and then documented as if it were in the callee.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Call `evaluate_gt(sim.contacts_public().iter().map(|c| c.at_ms).collect(), split)` directly (the obvious API use) on `pilot_partition_heal`, where `part*part` contacts share `heal_at_ms` — with enough duplicates the median interval becomes 0, clamped to 1.0 ms by `predictor.rs:99`, and every prediction is off by a full period.
- **Impact:** GT timing error becomes meaningless for any caller that does not know the undocumented precondition; AC-4's "GT beats static" result is caller-dependent.
- **Fix:** Add `sorted.dedup();` after `experiment.rs:156` and `times.dedup();` after `predictor.rs:84`, and state the postcondition in the doc comment. Also guard `intervals.is_empty()` after dedup.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/ml/predictor.rs`, `tests/ml_experiments.rs:130-139` (the helper's dedup becomes redundant but harmless).

#### SIM-17: `route2_opportunistic_matches_delivery_with_lower_overhead` never asserts overhead — and no test anywhere reads `overhead_ratio`
- **Severity:** High
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/tests/sim_scenarios.rs:174-192`; metric defined at `crates/iris-core/src/sim/metrics.rs:42-43,85-89,117-120`
- **What:** The test's name and doc comment promise the ROUTE-002 headline claim ("should lower the overhead ratio"). Its three assertions check delivery-not-degraded, loop-free, and delivery > 0.5. `overhead_ratio` is never compared between the L0 and L2 arms — indeed `grep -rn "\.overhead()\|overhead_ratio" crates/ --include=*.rs` finds only the three definition sites in `metrics.rs` and no reader at all.
- **Evidence:**
```
sim_scenarios.rs:175    // Sparse community + ferry mobility. L2 (DP + spray) must not reduce
sim_scenarios.rs:176    // delivery vs L0/SCF baseline, and should lower the overhead ratio.
sim_scenarios.rs:178    let base = run_ferry(7, false);
sim_scenarios.rs:179    let l2 = run_ferry(7, true);
sim_scenarios.rs:180    assert!(l2.delivery_ratio >= base.delivery_ratio - 0.05, ...);
sim_scenarios.rs:186    assert!(l2.loop_free, "L2 must stay loop-free");
sim_scenarios.rs:188    assert!(l2.delivery_ratio > 0.5, ...);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** ROUTE2_DESIGN.md's acceptance is "match L0 delivery at lower overhead". Half of that acceptance criterion has no executable check. `SimMetrics::overhead()` (metrics.rs:118) is dead code.
- **Root cause:** The overhead assertion was presumably dropped when it failed and the delivery-only assertions were kept.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Make `opportunistic_forward` return `true` unconditionally (pure epidemic flooding — the exact thing GTMX+ exists to prevent). Delivery goes up, loop_free holds, and this test passes.
- **Impact:** ROUTE-002's entire value proposition is unverified. Combined with SIM-11 (no forwarding-outcome counters) there is no signal at all that the opportunistic layer is doing anything useful.
- **Fix:** Add `assert!(l2.overhead() < base.overhead(), "L2={} L0={}", l2.overhead(), base.overhead());` and record both numbers in ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md. If it fails, that failure is the finding.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `tests/sim_scenarios.rs`, ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md.

#### SIM-18: `overhead_ratio` returns 0.0 — the best possible value — when nothing was delivered
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/metrics.rs:85-89` (fn `from_outcome`)
- **What:** The guard against division by zero substitutes the *optimum* for "undefined". A run that relays 10 000 times and delivers nothing reports overhead 0.0, indistinguishable from a perfect run.
- **Evidence:**
```
metrics.rs:85            overhead_ratio: if out.delivered_total == 0 {
metrics.rs:86                0.0
metrics.rs:87            } else {
metrics.rs:88                out.relays_total as f64 / out.delivered_total as f64
metrics.rs:89            },
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Lower overhead is better, so the sentinel must be pessimistic (`f64::INFINITY`) or absent (`Option<f64>`). The same anti-pattern appears in `SimOutcome::delivered_ratio_for` (mod.rs:746) and `PrioritySlice::ratio` (metrics.rs:21-25), where 0.0 for "no samples" is at least conservative — here it is inverted.
- **Root cause:** Copy of the divide-by-zero idiom used for the delivery ratios, where 0.0 happens to be the safe direction.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Any total-partition scenario, or the SIM-17 fix landing on a scenario that delivers nothing — the assertion would pass on total failure.
- **Impact:** Once an overhead assertion exists (SIM-17), a catastrophic-failure run silently satisfies it.
- **Fix:** `overhead_ratio: Option<f64>`, or `f64::INFINITY` for the zero-delivery case, and require callers to check `delivered_total > 0` first.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/metrics.rs`, any future overhead assertion.

#### SIM-19: Percentile index uses `round()` on `(n-1)*p`, so `p95` of 20 samples returns the 90th percentile
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/metrics.rs:123-132` (fn `percentiles`)
- **What:** `idx = ((n-1) * p/100).round()`. For n=20, p=95: `19*0.95 = 18.05 → round → 18`, i.e. `sorted[18]`, the 19th of 20 values — the empirical 90th percentile (`18/19 = 0.947` by the linear-interpolation convention, and only 1 of 20 samples lies above it). Rounding *down* on a 0.05 fraction systematically under-reports the tail. Symmetrically, `p50` of an even-length list returns the upper-middle element rather than the mean of the two middles: the module's own test asserts `percentiles(&[1,2,3,4], 50, 95) == (3, 4)`, i.e. a "median" of 3 for data whose median is 2.5.
- **Evidence:**
```
metrics.rs:127      let at = |p: f64| {
metrics.rs:128          let idx = ((sorted.len() as f64 - 1.0) * p / 100.0).round() as usize;
metrics.rs:129          sorted[idx]
metrics.rs:130      };
metrics.rs:162        assert_eq!(percentiles(&[1, 2, 3, 4], 50.0, 95.0), (3, 4));
```
- **Why it is wrong:** p95 is a *tail* statistic used as a pass/fail gate (`scenario.rs:455` asserts `latency_p95_ms <= 30_000`). Rounding to nearest biases the tail downward at exactly the sample sizes the pilot uses (N=20/50/100), making the gate easier than specified. There is also no interpolation, so p95 can never exceed the 19th of 20 observed latencies.
- **Root cause:** Nearest-rank was chosen for simplicity without picking a named percentile convention.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** 20 latencies, 19 at 1000 ms and one at 120 000 ms. True p95 (linear interpolation, R-7) is ~113 000 ms; this returns 1000 ms and the `<= 30_000` gate passes.
- **Impact:** `pilot_b1_nct_of_n_delivers_all_with_latency_cdf` (scenario.rs:441-461) reports a latency CDF that is optimistic in exactly the tail the PILOT KPI plan cares about. Note this compounds with SIM-8 — the latencies being percentiled are contact-schedule artefacts to begin with.
- **Fix:** Use the R-7 / linear-interpolation convention and `ceil` for tail percentiles:
```rust
let at = |p: f64| {
    let rank = (sorted.len() as f64 - 1.0) * p / 100.0;
    let lo = rank.floor() as usize; let hi = rank.ceil() as usize;
    let frac = rank - lo as f64;
    (sorted[lo] as f64 * (1.0 - frac) + sorted[hi] as f64 * frac).round() as u64
};
```
Update `percentile_edge_cases` (metrics.rs:158-163) to expect `(2, 4)` for `[1,2,3,4]`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/metrics.rs`, `scenario.rs:454-455`, PILOT_KPI_PLAN.md latency thresholds.

#### SIM-20: `wilson_ci_95` produces silent `NaN` when `k > n`, and never validates its inputs
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/metrics.rs:138-152` (fn `wilson_ci_95`)
- **What:** With `k > n`, `p = k/n > 1`, so `p*(1-p) < 0` and the `.sqrt()` yields `NaN`. `NaN.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` returns `NaN` (clamp only panics when `min > max`), so both bounds silently become `NaN` and every subsequent comparison — including the pass/fail assertion — evaluates to `false`.
- **Evidence:**
```
metrics.rs:144      let p = k as f64 / n;
metrics.rs:147      let margin = (z * ((p * (1.0 - p)) / n + z2 / (4.0 * n * n)).sqrt()) / (1.0 + z2 / n);
metrics.rs:149          (centre - margin).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
metrics.rs:150          (centre + margin).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The doc comment (metrics.rs:134-137) calls the lower bound "the pass/fail statistic". `k > n` is reachable: `SimOutcome.delivered_total` counts entries in every node's `delivered` vec while `injected_total` counts injections; if a duplicate terminal delivery ever occurs (exactly the bug `loop_free()` exists to detect), `delivered_total > injected_total` and `wilson_ci_95(out.delivered_total, out.injected_total)` at `scenario.rs:456,477` goes NaN.
- **Root cause:** The `n == 0` degenerate case was handled; the `k > n` one was not considered because the caller "cannot" produce it.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A routing regression causing one duplicate delivery in `pilot_b1_nct_of_n_scales_to_100` makes `assert!(lo >= 0.90 && hi <= 1.0)` fail with a confusing `NaN` message instead of the real duplicate-delivery diagnosis — or, at `scenario.rs:460`, `assert!(lo > 0.80 && lo < 0.90)` fails opaquely.
- **Root cause / Fix:** Clamp at the top: `let k = k.min(n_usize);` plus a `debug_assert!(k <= n)`, and return `(0.0, 1.0)` for the degenerate case rather than `(0.0, 0.0)` — an empty sample bounds nothing, and `(0.0, 0.0)` currently claims a *tight* interval at zero, which `assert!(lo >= 0.90)` would report as a delivery failure rather than as "no data".
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/scenario.rs:456,477`, PILOT_001 KPI evidence.

#### SIM-21: OBSERVABILITY.md promises gauges, a latency histogram and priority labels; the implementation ships bare counters with no labels
- **Severity:** High

Promised-but-missing, verbatim from the doc: `iris_delivery_ratio` (gauge), `iris_messages_in_queue` (gauge, per priority), `iris_transport_active` (gauge, per transport), `iris_ack_timeout_total` (counter), `iris_storage_usage_bytes` (gauge), `iris_neighbor_count` (gauge), `iris_routing_table_size` (gauge), and `iris_message_delivery_latency_ms` (**histogram**, per priority). The naming grammar also diverges: the doc uses `iris_x_y`, the code uses `iris.x.y` (mod.rs:126).
- **Evidence:**
```

OBSERVABILITY.md:152        "iris_message_delivery_latency_ms",
OBSERVABILITY.md:154        "End-to-end message delivery latency when ack is received"
OBSERVABILITY.md:166    histogram!("iris_message_delivery_latency_ms", "priority" => priority.to_string())

```
- **Why it is wrong:** `mod.rs:166-167` documents that "Labels are low-cardinality (`MessagePriority`, routing algorithm, gateway id) and bounded" — there is no label mechanism in the type at all, so the sentence describes a design that was never built. Without gauges there is no queue depth, storage usage, neighbour count or transport-liveness signal; without the histogram there is no delivery-latency distribution, which is the single most operationally important mesh metric and the one the doc's own sample dashboard prints ("Avg latency", "P99 latency", OBSERVABILITY.md:269-270).
- **Root cause:** The `metrics` crate dependency in the doc was replaced by a hand-rolled lock-free registry (for the no-global-state / P6 constraints) and only the counter subset was carried over.

#### SIM-22: `MetricsRegistry::increment` silently discards unknown metric names, and a test enshrines that as a feature
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/observability/mod.rs:219-231`, test at `mod.rs:296-297`
- **What:** `increment`/`add` do `if let Some(c) = self.inner.counters.get(name)` and otherwise do nothing — no error, no return value, no debug assertion. A metric name that was never pre-registered in `MetricsRegistry::new` (mod.rs:191-211) is a silent no-op.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:220      pub fn increment(&self, name: &'static str) {
mod.rs:221          if let Some(c) = self.inner.counters.get(name) {
mod.rs:222              c.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
mod.rs:223          }
mod.rs:296          // Unknown names are silently ignored — default-deny (P3).
mod.rs:297          reg.increment("iris.unknown.name");
```
- **Why it is wrong:** P3 default-deny is about *attributes on events*, not about swallowing counter writes. Because every call site passes a `&'static str` constant from `mod::metric`, the only way to hit this path is a genuine bug — adding a new `pub const` to `mod metric` and forgetting to add it to the `new()` array. That mistake then produces a counter that reads 0 forever with no diagnostic.
- **Root cause:** The lookup-then-ignore idiom was reused from a lenient API and rationalised as a privacy control.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** The `metric` module has 19 constants and `new()` registers 19 (asserted at mod.rs:299) — they currently match by luck plus one hand-maintained magic number. Add a 20th constant, wire it into `message_engine`, forget `new()`: the counter silently stays 0 and only the unrelated `assert_eq!(reg.snapshot().len(), 19)` would fail, which a developer will "fix" by bumping the number.
- **Impact:** Silent telemetry loss for any newly added metric — the failure mode is "the dashboard shows zero", which reads as "the event never happened".
- **Fix:** Drive both the constant list and the registration array from one source (a macro or a `pub const ALL: &[&str]` used by `new()` and asserted against in a test), and add `debug_assert!(self.inner.counters.contains_key(name), "unregistered metric {name}")` inside `increment`/`add`.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `observability/mod.rs:126-160,187-217,288-300`.

#### SIM-24: P5 "bounded retention" is a comment, not a mechanism — `reset()` has no caller
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/observability/mod.rs:15-16` (privacy contract P5), `mod.rs:242-252` (fn `reset`)
- **What:** The module header lists "P5: bounded retention (7-day metric window per OBSERVABILITY.md)" as a *hard constraint*. The implementation is a `reset()` method whose own doc comment admits "v1 ships no in-crate rotation timer; the contract lives here". `grep -rn "\.reset()" crates/` finds only the unit test at mod.rs:305.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:15   //! - P5: bounded retention (7-day metric window per OBSERVABILITY.md).
mod.rs:244  /// This is the OBSERVABILITY.md P5 retention hook: the embedding host is
mod.rs:245  /// expected to call `reset()` at least once per 7-day window (e.g. in the
mod.rs:247  /// v1 ships no in-crate rotation timer; the contract lives here.
mod.rs:248  pub fn reset(&self) {
```
- **Why it is wrong:** A privacy constraint discharged by hoping the embedder calls a method is not a constraint. Neither `iris-android/src/engine.rs`, `iris-ios/src/engine.rs` nor `iris-desktop/src/engine_handle.rs` — the three embedders that hold a `MetricsRegistry` — call `reset()`. So in practice counters accumulate for the lifetime of the process with no window at all.
- **Root cause:** Deliberate scope cut, honestly documented in the doc comment but not reflected in the header's "hard constraints" list.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A long-lived daemon accumulates monotonic counters indefinitely; a 7-day retention claim in a privacy review is unsupportable.
- **Impact:** Compliance/claims risk more than technical risk (`u64` will not overflow in any realistic lifetime — see verified-safe). The claim in the header is currently false.
- **Fix:** Either spawn the rotation task in the crate (a `tokio::time::interval` in the engine that calls `reset()` and flushes), or downgrade P5 in the header to "P5 (host responsibility): the embedder MUST call `reset()` per window" and add the call to all three embedders.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `iris-android/src/engine.rs`, `iris-ios/src/engine.rs`, `iris-desktop/src/engine_handle.rs`, `OBS_VERIFICATION.md` P5 evidence.

#### SIM-25: The P3 "default-deny attribute allow-list" does not exist — `tracing` call sites pass free-form fields with no enforcement
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/observability/mod.rs:13-14,70-71` (claim) vs call sites e.g. `crates/iris-core/src/message_engine/mod.rs:486-489`, `crates/iris-core/src/routing/mod.rs:210-213`
- **What:** The header states "P3: default-deny attribute allow-list — fields come from this module's event registry, not free-form caller attributes", and `mod event` (mod.rs:70-72) says the taxonomy is "Centralized so the allow-list of attributes per event lives in one place (privacy P3)". In reality `mod event` contains only `&'static str` *event names*. There is no per-event field list, no macro wrapper, and no compile-time or runtime check: every call site writes raw `tracing::info!(event = event::X, arbitrary_field = ..., ...)`.
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:13   //! - P3: default-deny attribute allow-list — fields come from this module's
mod.rs:14   //!   event registry, not free-form caller attributes.
mod.rs:72   pub mod event {
mod.rs:73       pub const MSG_CREATED: &str = "msg.created";
message_engine/mod.rs:486            event = event::MSG_CREATED,
message_engine/mod.rs:487            message_id = %envelope.message_id.short(),
message_engine/mod.rs:489            size_bytes = envelope.payload.len(),
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The same header asserts (mod.rs:26-29) that `ShortId` "is the only type the event registry accepts for identifiers, [so] a full 16/32-byte ID cannot appear in any log/event/metric field **by construction** (OBS-RT-01)". Nothing constructs anything: a call site can write `peer = ?peer_id` (full 32 bytes via `Debug`) or `body = %String::from_utf8_lossy(&envelope.payload)` and it compiles, passes clippy, and ships. The privacy guarantee rests on reviewer discipline, and is stated in the code as if it were mechanically enforced.
- **Root cause:** The constants module was intended to grow into a typed event API (`fn emit(event: Event, fields: Fields)`) and stopped at string constants.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Any future `tracing::debug!` added during debugging that interpolates `envelope.payload` or a full `PeerId`. Nothing in CI catches it. Note `message_engine/mod.rs:489` already logs `size_bytes` — benign, but it is a free-form attribute, proving the allow-list is not real.
- **Impact:** P1 (no payload bytes) and P2 (truncated identifiers) are conventions, not invariants, in a codebase whose threat model is metadata exposure in a mesh. The audit statement "by construction" is unearned.
- **Fix:** Make it structural: a `macro_rules! iris_event!` that accepts only a known event const plus a fixed field set per event, or at minimum a CI grep denying `\.payload`, `?peer`, `?envelope`, `{:?}` on identity types inside `tracing::` macros, plus a `#[deny]` lint. Until then, correct the header to say "convention, reviewer-enforced".
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** every `tracing::` call site in `message_engine/`, `routing/`, `gateway/`; `OBS_VERIFICATION.md` OBS-RT-01 evidence.

#### SIM-26: Truncated but stable peer pseudonyms in routing and security logs let a log holder reconstruct the social graph
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** High
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/routing/mod.rs:210-213` (`ROUTE_DECISION`), `crates/iris-core/src/message_engine/mod.rs:617-618,634-636,660-661,674-675` (SEC-001 events)
- **What:** Every routing decision logs the *recipient* identity, and the security events log the *sender* identity, as an 8-byte prefix. The prefix is deterministic and collision-free in practice (2^64), so it is a stable pseudonym, not an anonymisation. A node's log therefore contains a timestamped edge list: "at T, this device made a forwarding decision toward peer `a3f1...`".
- **Evidence:**
```
routing/mod.rs:210        self.telemetry.increment(metric::ROUTING_DECISIONS_TOTAL);
routing/mod.rs:213            dest = %recipient.short(),
message_engine/mod.rs:617                    message_id = %envelope.message_id.short(),
message_engine/mod.rs:618                    sender = %hex::encode(sender_short),
message_engine/mod.rs:635                message_id = %envelope.message_id.short(),
message_engine/mod.rs:636                sender = %hex::encode(sender_short),
```
- **Why it is wrong:** P2 (mod.rs:11-12) treats truncation as the privacy control, but truncation to 8 bytes defends against *key recovery*, not against *linkage*. In a privacy-critical mesh the sensitive fact is usually "who communicated with whom, when" — precisely what a stable per-peer pseudonym plus a timestamp preserves. The taxonomy makes this a routine, always-on `INFO`/`WARN` field rather than an opt-in diagnostic.
- **Root cause:** P2 was specified as "truncate identifiers" and implemented literally; the linkage property was not analysed.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A seized or shared device log, or a crash-report upload, exposes the contact graph of the device owner even though no full key or payload appears.
- **Impact:** The strongest remaining metadata exposure in the observability layer. It is bounded (no payloads, no full ids, no locations — see verified-safe) but it is real and it is the one the threat model should care about most.
- **Fix:** Log peer identity only at `DEBUG`/`TRACE` (which P4 says is never enabled in production), or replace the raw prefix with a per-boot salted hash (`H(salt || peer_id)[..8]`) so pseudonyms do not correlate across sessions or across devices. Keep `message_id.short()` as-is — it is per-message and non-linking.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `routing/mod.rs`, `message_engine/mod.rs` SEC-001 events, `gateway/mod.rs:524,545` (gateway ids — lower risk, gateways are semi-public), threat model doc.

#### SIM-27: `ac1_no_shadow_is_zero_cost` never runs the no-shadow case, and `ac2`'s "byte-identical" assertion compares a trivially-true inequality
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/tests/ml_experiments.rs:74-99`
- **What:** Two of the three shadow-safety tests are hollow. `ac1_no_shadow_is_zero_cost` is documented "Without the observer the shadow vec is empty" but both of its bindings come from runs *with* an observer or from `ferry_l2_only` whose `shadow_samples` is never inspected — the no-shadow branch is never asserted. `ac2_shadow_run_is_byte_identical_to_l2_only` closes with `shadowed.shadow_samples.len() > base.shadow_samples.len()`, where `base` is an un-shadowed run whose vector is `Vec::new()` by construction (`sim/mod.rs:677`, `self.shadow.map(...).unwrap_or_default()`), so the comparison is `n > 0` dressed up as a comparison.
- **Evidence:**
```
ml_experiments.rs:75      // Without the observer the shadow vec is empty and the anchor matches the
ml_experiments.rs:78      let out = ferry_shadow(7);
ml_experiments.rs:79      let base = ferry_l2_only(7);
ml_experiments.rs:80      assert_eq!(out.result_anchor, base.result_anchor, "AC-2 anchor parity");
ml_experiments.rs:95      assert!(
ml_experiments.rs:96          shadowed.shadow_samples.len() > base.shadow_samples.len(),
ml_experiments.rs:97          "shadow run must record decisions"
```
- **Why it is wrong:** "Byte-identical" is asserted via `result_anchor`, which is two counters (SIM-2). The four supporting equalities (`delivered_total`, `relays_total`, `avg_hop_count`, `injected_total`) are aggregates that would survive a shadow observer perturbing *which* messages went where. ML_DESIGN.md §6 requires the L3 arm's forwarding to be identical to the L2 arm's — that is a per-decision claim and is checked only in aggregate.
- **Root cause:** The tests were written against the aggregates that `SimOutcome` happened to expose.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Make `shadow_features` (mod.rs:262-293) mutate node state — e.g. call `opp.p_for` through a `&mut` path that ages DPs. Delivery totals could easily stay identical while routes change; AC-2 stays green.
- **Impact:** The shadow-only guarantee — the entire safety argument for having an ML layer in a routing stack at all — rests on aggregate equality. Add `assert!(base.shadow_samples.is_empty())` and compare full delivery traces `(id, node, at_ms)`.
- **Fix:** In `ac1_no_shadow_is_zero_cost`, assert `ferry_l2_only(7).shadow_samples.is_empty()`. In `ac2`, compare sorted `(message_id, node_index, delivered_at)` triples between the two runs, not just counts (this rides on the SIM-2 trace-hash fix).
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `tests/ml_experiments.rs`, ML_VERIFICATION.md AC-1/AC-2 evidence.

#### SIM-28: `ac6_shadow_features_encode_priority_rank` and `ac3`'s Brier assertion are tautologies
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/tests/ml_experiments.rs:237-251` and `ml_experiments.rs:122-125`
- **What:** AC-6 claims to prove "the shadow feature extraction reads real in-band state and stays in sync with the message's priority", then asserts only `(0.0..=7.0).contains(&rank)`. Every message in `ferry_shadow` is injected as `MessagePriority::P4` (`inject_standard`, `scenario.rs:240`), so the true expected value is the constant `4.0`; the test would pass if slot 7 held a hard-coded `0.0`, or the buffer-occupancy value, or anything else in range. Separately, AC-3 asserts `(0.0..=1.0).contains(&m.brier_score)` — a Brier score is `mean((p-y)^2)` with `p ∈ (0,1)` and `y ∈ {0,1}`, so it is in `[0,1]` by definition, and the `MlMetrics::default()` early-return value is `1.0` (`experiment.rs:44`), which also satisfies it.
- **Evidence:**
```
ml_experiments.rs:245        let rank = s.features.as_slice()[7];
ml_experiments.rs:246        assert!(
ml_experiments.rs:247            (0.0..=7.0).contains(&rank),
ml_experiments.rs:248            "priority-rank feature must be in 0..=7, got {rank}"
ml_experiments.rs:122     assert!(
ml_experiments.rs:123         (0.0..=1.0).contains(&m.brier_score),
scenario.rs:240                    MessagePriority::P4,
```
- **Why it is wrong:** A range check on a value whose range is guaranteed by its type/definition tests nothing. The stated intent — "stays in sync with the message's priority" — requires a mixed-priority scenario and an exact comparison.
- **Root cause:** Assertions were loosened to whatever passed rather than to what the comment claims.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Swap slots 3 and 7 in `FeatureVec::new` (`sim/mod.rs:290-292`) so hop count lands in the priority slot — with P4 hop budget 3, hops are 0..3, inside `0..=7`, and the test still passes.
- **Impact:** ML-001 AC-6 provides no coverage; the feature-vector slot contract (documented at `sim/mod.rs:256-261`) is unverified. Combined with SIM-15/SIM-13, none of AC-3/AC-6 measures what its name claims.
- **Fix:** Inject a mix of P0/P2/P4 and assert `rank == s`'s actual envelope priority for each sample (requires carrying the priority on `ShadowDecision`, or asserting the exact set `{4.0}` for the current all-P4 scenario). Replace the Brier range check with a comparison against the base rate (`brier < p*(1-p)` for the observed delivery rate) — a model no better than the prior should fail.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `tests/ml_experiments.rs`, `sim/ml/mod.rs::ShadowDecision`.

#### SIM-29: `loss_reduces_delivery_ratio_monotonically` and `route2_spray_bounds_overhead_property` both pass when the mechanism they test is disabled
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/tests/sim_scenarios.rs:104-112` and `sim_scenarios.rs:201-238`
- **What:** (a) The loss test asserts `lossy <= zero` — a non-strict inequality, so `set_loss(loss(60.0))` having *no effect whatsoever* satisfies it. Given `set_loss` is the only failure knob the simulator has (SIM-8), the test that the knob works is the one test that cannot detect it being broken. (b) The spray test computes `relays_total / injected_total` — a **mean** across all messages — and asserts it is `<= L`. The binary-spray invariant it cites ("copies never exceed L **per message**") is a per-message bound; a mean cannot detect one message exploding to 10×L while others are quiet.
- **Evidence:**
```
sim_scenarios.rs:109      sim.set_loss(loss(60.0));
sim_scenarios.rs:111      assert!(lossy <= zero, "loss must not improve delivery");
sim_scenarios.rs:224      // AC-4: copies never exceed L per message (binary spray invariant).
sim_scenarios.rs:227      let handoffs_per_msg = out.relays_total as f64 / out.injected_total.max(1) as f64;
sim_scenarios.rs:228      assert!(
sim_scenarios.rs:229          handoffs_per_msg <= l as f64,
```
- **Why it is wrong:** The doc comment at sim_scenarios.rs:203 even says "per-message relays never exceed L×2" — three different bounds appear in one test (L×2 in the comment, L in the assertion, mean-of-L in the code). `SimNode.relays` (mod.rs:54) is a per-node counter with no message dimension, so the per-message bound is not computable from `SimOutcome` as it stands.
- **Root cause:** (a) A monotonicity test written defensively to avoid flakiness. (b) The available aggregate was substituted for the intended per-message statistic.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** Delete the `if self.is_lost() { return Blocked }` branch at `sim/mod.rs:372-374` — the loss test still passes. Make `SprayBudget::handoff` return `Some(L)` without halving (breaking the binary-spray invariant outright) — the mean stays low as long as most messages are delivered on their first contact, and the test still passes.
- **Impact:** The loss model and the spray bound, the two mechanisms with dedicated property tests, both have tests that cannot fail on their own regression.
- **Fix:** (a) `assert!(lossy < zero, ...)` with a seed chosen so the strict inequality holds, plus a second assertion that the drop is roughly in the expected band. (b) Track relays per `MessageId` (`HashMap<MessageId, u64>` on `SimOutcome`, populated where `relays` is incremented at mod.rs:401) and assert `max <= L` over messages.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/mod.rs:54,401` (needs a per-message relay tally), `tests/sim_scenarios.rs`, ROUTE2_VERIFICATION.md AC-4.

#### SIM-30: Per-node sim state grows unboundedly with message count — `hops_by_msg`, `spray`, and the dedup ring are never pruned
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Fix status:** ⬜ Not started  ·  Tier 3
- **Confidence:** Certain
- **Location:** `crates/iris-core/src/sim/mod.rs:45,52` (fields), inserted at `mod.rs:382,515,517,575`
- **What:** `SimNode.hops_by_msg: HashMap<MessageId, u8>` and `SimNode.spray: HashMap<MessageId, SprayBudget>` gain an entry per message per node and are never removed — not on terminal delivery, not on TTL expiry, not on eviction (which never happens anyway, SIM-5). The same is true of the `ForwardedCache` exact set and ring, whose only pruning path is real-time-gated and therefore inert in the sim (SIM-10).
- **Evidence:**
```
mod.rs:45      pub hops_by_msg: HashMap<MessageId, u8>,
mod.rs:52      pub spray: HashMap<MessageId, SprayBudget>,
mod.rs:382         self.nodes[dst].hops_by_msg.insert(id, new_hops);
mod.rs:515         a.spray.insert(id, SprayBudget::new(keep));
mod.rs:517         b.spray.insert(id, SprayBudget::new(give));
mod.rs:575         self.nodes[inj.from].hops_by_msg.insert(id, 0);
```
- **Why it is wrong:** Two consequences. (i) Scale: memory is `O(nodes × messages)` — `pilot_nct_of_n(100, 10, ·)` is 1000 messages over 100 nodes, fine, but the SCALE_TESTING ambition of thousands of nodes × long runs is not reachable. (ii) Correctness: `hops_by_msg` doubles as the **hop-budget state** (read at mod.rs:324), so a node that already relayed a message and later re-encounters it carries a permanent hop count. That is the intended anti-loop behaviour, but it also means the sim's hop accounting can never be reset the way a production node's would be after cache expiry — the same forgiveness as SIM-10, in a second place.
- **Root cause:** Sim bookkeeping was written as append-only because runs are short.
- **Trigger / failure scenario:** A long-horizon scale scenario (100 nodes, 100 k messages) exhausts memory; more subtly, hop-budget exhaustion in the sim is permanent whereas in production it is windowed.
- **Impact:** Blocks the SCALE_TESTING work and quietly makes the sim's anti-loop stronger than production's.
- **Fix:** Remove the `hops_by_msg` and `spray` entries when a message reaches terminal status at that node (alongside the `mark_forwarded(..., true)` calls at mod.rs:394-395), and prune on the virtual-clock TTL once SIM-4/SIM-10 land.
- **Dependencies / blast radius:** `sim/mod.rs` hop-budget semantics — changing this changes delivery outcomes; re-baseline all scenarios.
